Drugs target complementary symptomatic pathways of the common cold: brompheniramine (antihistamine) for nasal symptoms, dextromethorphan (antitussive) for cough suppression, and terpin hydrate (expectorant) to loosen mucus, producing combined symptomatic benefit.

Acetaminophen is the primary analgesic; phenyltoloxamine (an antihistamine with sedative/adjunct effects) can augment symptomatic relief for aches/pains. Role of ethanol is unclear (excipient vs. concomitant alcohol, potential interaction), so review is needed.

Urea is a keratolytic/humectant that restores skin barrier and hydration; hydrocortisone is an anti-inflammatory corticosteroid. Their complementary actions target different aspects of dermatitis pathology and can enhance topical treatment efficacy.
Ibuprofen is an NSAID used for RA symptoms; famotidine is an H2 blocker used to reduce NSAID-associated gastric acid/ulcer risk, mitigating side effects rather than enhancing RA treatment.

Mixture of essential-oil monoterpenes (borneol, eucalyptol, menthol/menthone, pinene isomers, camphene) are used as antispasmodic/choleretic/carminative agents to relieve biliary colic and improve gallbladder/bile flow, implying complementary mechanisms targeting gallbladder dysfunction.

Both entries are formulations/names of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine; vaccination prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection (a cause of ARDS) but does not represent a mechanistic combination therapy for treating adult ARDS. Indication mapping is ambiguous.
Clavulanic acid is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that can protect a beta-lactam antibiotic (ceftibuten) from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy against pathogens causing urethritis.
Both agents are potassium salts that provide potassium supplementation to correct hypokalemia via the same mechanism (replenishing serum K+).
Sulbactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects the β-lactam antibiotic ceftriaxone from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy against bacterial infections.

Mometasone (topical corticosteroid) reduces inflammation while terbinafine (antifungal) treats fungal etiology; together they address complementary mechanisms in dermatitis with a fungal/inflammatory component.

Tuaminoheptane is a topical decongestant (vasoconstrictor) reducing nasal mucosal swelling; acetylcysteine is a mucolytic that thins purulent secretions. Together they target complementary mechanisms to improve nasal patency and mucus clearance in purulent rhinitis.

Pancrelipase (digestive enzymes) and dimethicone (anti‑foaming for gas) have different symptomatic roles; relation to the indexed term ‘Oxygen’ is unclear and the combination’s mechanistic relationship or indication is ambiguous.

Rhubarb (a laxative/ GI motility agent) could address underlying gastrointestinal causes of abdominal pain while salicylic acid has analgesic/anti-inflammatory properties; together they act on complementary mechanisms to relieve abdominal pain.

Acetaminophen is an analgesic/antipyretic and scopolamine is an antimuscarinic antiemetic/antispasmodic; neither targets bleeding mechanisms or clearly relieves the other's adverse effects. No clear mechanistic synergy or comorbidity rationale present.

Lidocaine and procaine are local anesthetics providing analgesia while oxyquinoline is an antiseptic/antibacterial; together they address pain control and infection prevention in superficial wound treatment.

Fluocinolone is a topical corticosteroid (anti-inflammatory) and Ketocaine is a local anesthetic/analgesic; together they address inflammatory pathology and symptomatic pain/itch in anal eczema via complementary mechanisms.

Drugs target complementary symptom pathways of the common cold: guaifenesin (expectorant/mucus clearance), phenylephrine (nasal decongestant via α-agonism), and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic), providing combined symptomatic benefit.

Diphenhydramine (antihistamine) and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) target complementary symptom pathways of the common cold (nasal/sneezing vs pain/fever), providing combined symptomatic relief.

Drugs target complementary symptomatic mechanisms for common cold: ascorbic acid (immune/antioxidant), acetylcysteine (mucolytic/antioxidant, reduces sputum viscosity), and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic), providing multi-pathway symptomatic relief.

Phenylephrine (decongestant), ibuprofen (NSAID analgesic/antipyretic), and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) act on complementary symptomatic pathways in the common cold, providing additive symptom relief.

Phenylephrine (nasal decongestant), chlorphenamine (antihistamine) and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) act on different pathways to relieve complementary symptoms of the common cold, representing multi-target symptomatic therapy.

Both sulfur and salicylic acid are topical keratolytic/comedolytic agents used to treat acne; they target overlapping processes (exfoliation, reduction of hyperkeratinization and comedone formation) and can have complementary antibacterial/anti-inflammatory effects, enhancing acne treatment.
These agents are components of IV fluid resuscitation/volume expanders (crystalloids and colloid) and electrolytes used together to restore intravascular volume and correct electrolytes in shock.

Tasonermin (recombinant TNF-α) is used with melphalan in isolated limb perfusion for soft tissue sarcoma; TNF-α increases tumor vascular permeability and potentiates melphalan cytotoxicity, producing synergistic antitumor effects.

Lazertinib is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and amivantamab is a bispecific EGFR/MET antibody; together they target EGFR via complementary modalities and also address MET-mediated resistance, producing synergistic effects in NSCLC.

Cedazuridine is a cytidine deaminase inhibitor that prevents decitabine metabolism, increasing decitabine exposure/oral bioavailability; combined formulation enhances decitabine therapeutic effect in myelodysplasia.

Dexamethasone (anti-inflammatory corticosteroid) plus clotrimazole (antifungal) and framycetin (topical aminoglycoside antibiotic) address inflammation and possible fungal/bacterial infection in dermatitis via complementary mechanisms.

Methotrexate (antifolate/DMARD) and cyclosporine (calcineurin inhibitor) are complementary immunosuppressants used together to enhance control of rheumatoid arthritis by targeting distinct immune pathways.

Dexketoprofen is an NSAID analgesic; acetylcysteine is a mucolytic/antioxidant used mainly for acetaminophen toxicity and respiratory mucus. There is no clear, established mechanistic synergy for treating abdominal pain and the combination likely reflects unrelated indications or is unclear.
Orphenadrine is a muscle relaxant/analgesic and ibuprofen is an NSAID; together they provide complementary analgesic mechanisms (muscle relaxation + anti-inflammatory analgesia) for abdominal pain.
Thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant reducing spasms; ibuprofen is an NSAID providing analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects. Together they target different mechanisms contributing to abdominal pain.

Icosapent ethyl lowers triglycerides, but mechanism/indication for Doconexent (CHEBI:28125) is unclear from available info; cannot determine if combination is synergistic, for side-effect relief, or due to comorbidity.

Calcium salts are supplements, not therapies for levothyroxine’s indication; they may reflect co‑treatment for bone health or cause a drug–drug absorption interaction with levothyroxine. Mechanistic relationship to the indexed condition is ambiguous.

Trastuzumab deruxtecan and pertuzumab are anti-HER2 oncology agents and hyaluronidase is an enzyme used to aid drug dispersion/subcutaneous delivery; none are treatments for high-risk pregnancy and anti-HER2 agents are typically contraindicated in pregnancy. Likely a mapping/error or unrelated combination, so insufficient/ambiguous for mechanistic classification.

Metronidazole + ceftazidime/avibactam are antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections or surgical prophylaxis, not anti-neoplastic agents for gestational trophoblastic neoplasms; likely used for infection management rather than tumor-directed therapy.

These four drugs comprise an anti-myeloma regimen (carfilzomib, daratumumab±hyaluronidase for subcutaneous delivery, dexamethasone); they are not antihypertensive agents nor do they mechanistically treat resistant hypertension. Mapping appears erroneous or outside intended categories.

Carfilzomib and daratumumab are anti-myeloma agents and dexamethasone is a steroid; none are standard treatments for resistant hypertension. This combination likely reflects treatment of comorbid malignancy rather than a coordinated mechanism to treat resistant hypertension.

condition_label: homocystinuria due to methylene tetrahydrofolate reductase deficiency
rationale_short: Drugs target complementary homocysteine-lowering pathways: betaine provides an alternative methyl donor via BHMT; folic acid and cobalamin support methionine synthase-dependent remethylation; pyridoxine is a cofactor for CBS-mediated transsulfuration—together lower homocysteine in MTHFR deficiency.

Pilocarpine (muscarinic agonist) increases trabecular outflow via miosis/ciliary muscle contraction; epinephrine (adrenergic) reduces aqueous humour production and can enhance outflow—complementary mechanisms lowering IOP in open‑angle glaucoma.

Macitentan (endothelin receptor antagonist) and tadalafil (PDE5 inhibitor) are primarily used for pulmonary hypertension; there is no clear, established synergistic anti-tumor mechanism for ependymoma linking these agents. Indication appears uncertain or off-label, so classification is ambiguous.

All three drugs increase inhibitory/GABAergic signaling (clobazam = GABA-A PAM, valproate increases GABA, stiripentol enhances GABAergic transmission and raises clobazam levels), producing complementary/pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic augmentation to reduce disinhibition.

Perindopril (ACE inhibitor) and amlodipine (calcium-channel blocker) provide complementary blood-pressure–lowering mechanisms; atorvastatin reduces lipid-driven atherosclerotic risk. Together they target multiple pathways relevant to hypertension/CV disease.

Enoxaparin (LMWH) provides immediate anticoagulation while warfarin provides delayed, long‑term oral anticoagulation; used together as bridging therapy for pulmonary embolism targeting the coagulation pathway.

Bovine type I collagen and neonatal foreskin keratinocytes are biomaterials/cell-based products used for tissue repair; it is unclear if they are intended as direct anti-neoplastic agents for mouth neoplasm or for post-surgical reconstruction, so mechanism/intent is ambiguous.

Acetaminophen and aspirin provide analgesia via complementary mechanisms (central analgesia vs. COX inhibition) and caffeine is a known adjuvant that potentiates analgesic effects; this combination is used OTC for pain relief.

Leucovorin (folinic acid) replaces folate for folate-deficiency anemia; ferric cation supplies iron for iron-deficiency anemia. They address different nutrient deficiencies likely co-occurring rather than synergizing on the same folate-related pathway.

Atezolizumab is an anti‑PD‑L1 immunotherapy; hyaluronidase degrades extracellular hyaluronan to alter tissue permeability. While hyaluronidase can theoretically improve drug/tumor penetration and thus immunotherapy access, this mechanism is not established for unresectable alveolar soft part sarcoma and the combination’s rationale is ambiguous.

Pembrolizumab (anti‑PD‑1) and enfortumab vedotin (Nectin‑4 ADC) target complementary antitumor mechanisms—immune checkpoint blockade plus direct ADC cytotoxicity—used together in urothelial carcinoma to enhance efficacy.

Trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (co-trimoxazole) inhibit sequential steps in bacterial folate synthesis, producing synergistic bactericidal activity against susceptible bacteria; used as an antibacterial regimen for enteric infections including cholera in some settings.

Rosuvastatin (statin) and olmesartan (ARB) are cardiovascular drugs for hyperlipidemia and hypertension; carcinosarcoma is a malignancy with no well-established synergistic anticancer mechanism for this drug pair, so co-prescription likely reflects comorbid cardiovascular conditions.

Diosmin and citrus bioflavonoids are venoactive flavonoids used together to improve venous tone, reduce capillary permeability and inflammation in chronic venous insufficiency, acting on complementary aspects of the same disease mechanism.

Triamcinolone is a corticosteroid for allergic inflammation; fusidic acid is an antibiotic for bacterial infection. Their pairing likely addresses concurrent/secondary bacterial infection in allergic skin conditions rather than synergistic anti-allergy mechanisms.

Baricitinib + remdesivir is an antiviral + host-directed anti-inflammatory combo used for COVID-19; there is no clear mechanistic or clinical rationale for this combination to treat or prevent psychiatric hospitalization.

Cilgavimab and tixagevimab are co-administered as a dual monoclonal antibody cocktail (Evusheld) providing complementary neutralization of SARS-CoV-2, targeting the same disease mechanism (viral entry) and reducing resistance—mechanistic synergy.

Dostarlimab is an anti‑PD‑1 immunotherapy and carboplatin+paclitaxel are cytotoxic chemotherapies; chemotherapy can increase tumor antigen release and immunogenicity, complementing checkpoint blockade to enhance anti‑tumor effects in recurrent endometrial cancer.

Ivosidenib is an IDH1 inhibitor and azacitidine is a hypomethylating agent commonly combined in IDH1‑mutant AML; there is no clear, established mechanistic rationale for this combination specifically in newly diagnosed childhood ependymoma. Evidence is ambiguous/off‑label.

Mechanisms of Nogapendekin alfa and Inbakicept are unclear/ambiguous relative to BCG and skin carcinoma in situ; combination could be immunomodulatory, antagonistic, or indicate comorbidity. Insufficient reliable mechanistic information to classify as synergistic, side-effect relief, or common comorbidity.

Pembrolizumab (anti‑PD‑1) combined with cytotoxic chemotherapy (cisplatin + gemcitabine) is mechanistically complementary: chemo induces tumor cell death/antigen release and may enhance responsiveness to checkpoint inhibition; cisplatin+gemcitabine is a standard biliary tract cancer backbone.

Betamethasone is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation; Isopto Cetamide is used as an ophthalmic antimicrobial/antiseptic—together they address infection and inflammatory response in bacterial blepharitis.

Aspirin (antiplatelet via COX‑1 inhibition) and enoxaparin (anticoagulant—LMWH inhibiting factor Xa/IIa) act on complementary components of thrombus formation, providing additive antithrombotic effects in myocardial ischemia/ACS.

List includes a known contact allergen (Balsam of Peru), topical antiseptics/protectants (boric acid, zinc oxide) and algeldrate (an antacid); mixture contains both potential causes and symptomatic skin agents, so mechanism for treating exanthem is unclear/ambiguous.
Acetaminophen provides analgesia while orphenadrine is a muscle relaxant; together they target pain and muscle spasm in whiplash via complementary mechanisms.

Theophylline is a bronchodilator used for asthma; chlorphenamine (antihistamine) and phenylephrine (decongestant) primarily treat allergic rhinitis/nasal congestion rather than directly enhancing asthma mechanisms, suggesting treatment of comorbid upper-airway allergic symptoms.
Both agents (hypromellose and dextran sulfate) are used in ophthalmic lubricants/viscometic formulations to stabilize the tear film and protect the ocular surface, jointly relieving eye irritation.

Combination includes bronchodilators (methoxyphenamine, aminophylline) plus an antihistamine (chlorphenamine) and an antitussive (noscapine), addressing complementary pathogenic/symptomatic mechanisms in asthma.
Tramadol (opioid/monoamine reuptake inhibitor) and acetaminophen (central analgesic) have complementary, additive analgesic mechanisms and are commonly combined to enhance pain relief in acute pain.
Fluticasone is an inhaled corticosteroid that reduces airway inflammation; salmeterol is a long-acting β2-agonist that provides bronchodilation. Their complementary mechanisms enhance asthma control.

Etafedrine (sympathomimetic bronchodilator) and theophylline (PDE inhibitor bronchodilator) produce complementary bronchodilation via cAMP-related mechanisms; guaifenesin aids mucus clearance—together act on airway obstruction in asthma.

Combination includes anti-inflammatory (prednisolone), antiseptic/antimicrobial agents (ichthammol, carvacrol/Carvasept) and a topical analgesic/cooling agent (levomenthol) addressing inflammation, microbial contributors and symptomatic itch—complementary mechanisms for treating pruritus ani.

Sofosbuvir (NS5B polymerase inhibitor) and Ledipasvir (NS5A inhibitor) directly target complementary steps in HCV replication and are co-formulated/approved (Harvoni) for chronic HCV genotype 1, producing mechanistic synergy.

Phenylephrine is an ocular vasoconstrictor reducing redness; boric acid acts as a mild antiseptic/buffering/soothing agent in eye preparations—distinct complementary mechanisms addressing eye irritation.

Combination contains multiple direct-acting antivirals targeting distinct HCV proteins (NS5A: ombitasvir; NS3/4A: paritaprevir; NS5B: dasabuvir) plus ribavirin as adjunct antiviral and ritonavir as a pharmacokinetic booster—agents act together to increase antiviral efficacy against HCV genotype 1a.

ICS (fluticasone) reduces airway inflammation while LABA (vilanterol) and LAMA (umeclidinium) provide complementary bronchodilation via β2 agonism and muscarinic blockade — combined therapy targets multiple COPD pathophysiologic mechanisms.

Elexacaftor and tezacaftor are CFTR correctors (improve folding/trafficking) and ivacaftor is a potentiator (increases channel gating); together they synergistically restore CFTR function in cystic fibrosis (approved triple therapy).
Olodaterol (LABA) and tiotropium (LAMA) are complementary long-acting bronchodilators that target different pathways to produce additive bronchodilation and improve COPD outcomes.

Elexacaftor and tezacaftor are CFTR correctors (improve folding/trafficking) and ivacaftor is a potentiator (increases channel gating); together they synergistically restore CFTR function in cystic fibrosis (approved triple therapy).

Ciclesonide (inhaled corticosteroid) reduces airway inflammation while carmoterol (long-acting β2-agonist) provides bronchodilation; combined ICS+LABA therapy is a standard synergistic approach to improve lung function and reduce exacerbations in COPD.
Tiotropium (LAMA) provides bronchodilation while budesonide (inhaled corticosteroid) reduces airway inflammation; complementary mechanisms commonly combined to treat COPD.

Budesonide (inhaled corticosteroid) reduces airway inflammation while formoterol (long-acting β2-agonist) provides bronchodilation; combined ICS+LABA therapy targets complementary pathways to improve lung function and reduce COPD exacerbations.
Formoterol (LABA) and aclidinium (LAMA) provide complementary bronchodilation via β2-agonism and muscarinic blockade, respectively, enhancing airflow in COPD.

Topical hydrocortisone is an anti-inflammatory corticosteroid while clioquinol is a topical antimicrobial/antifungal; together they address inflammation and secondary infection in stasis dermatitis, complementary mechanisms for the same condition.

Cetylpyridinium is an antiseptic/antimicrobial for oral mucosa; lidocaine is a topical local anesthetic for symptom relief. They address infection and pain separately rather than synergistically targeting the same disease mechanism, and lidocaine does not mitigate adverse effects of the antiseptic.

Magaldrate is an antacid used for acid-related ulcer symptoms; dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent added to reduce gas/bloating (a common adverse/symptomatic effect of antacid therapy), so dimethicone primarily mitigates side effects rather than synergistically treating duodenal ulcer.

Diflucortolone valerate is a topical corticosteroid that reduces mucosal inflammation; josamycin is an antibiotic addressing bacterial infection. Together they target complementary pathways (inflammation and infection) relevant to denture stomatitis.

Pseudoephedrine is a nasal decongestant; dextromethorphan is an antitussive. They treat different symptoms (decongestion vs cough) rather than synergistically targeting the mechanism of nasal sinus congestion or relieving each other's side effects.

Corticosteroids (triamcinolone, methylprednisolone) reduce inflammation in affected joints/spine while local anesthetics (bupivacaine, lidocaine) provide immediate analgesia; used together (e.g., injections) to treat ankylosing spondylitis symptoms via complementary mechanisms.

drug_labels: ['Human papillomavirus type 16 L1 capsid protein antigen', 'Human papillomavirus type 18 L1 capsid protein antigen']
rationale_short: HPV16 and HPV18 L1 antigens are combined in vaccines to induce immunity against multiple HPV types, jointly preventing infection/disease via complementary immune targeting of the same pathogenic family.

Demeclocycline is an antibiotic targeting bacterial infection; triamcinolone is a corticosteroid reducing local inflammation/symptoms. They act on complementary pathways (antimicrobial + anti-inflammatory) to address dental disease manifestations.

Chlorphenamine (H1 antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated allergic bronchospasm/symptoms while triamcinolone (corticosteroid) reduces airway inflammation; together they target complementary pathways in reactive airway disease.

Piperacillin is a β-lactam antibiotic and tazobactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects and extends piperacillin's activity against bacteria commonly involved in animal bite infections, producing complementary antimicrobial effects.

Cholecalciferol (vitamin D) and vitamin A are distinct nutrient supplements; vitamin A treats vitamin A deficiency while cholecalciferol addresses vitamin D deficiency. Their co-use likely reflects co-supplementation for concurrent nutritional deficiencies rather than a synergistic mechanism for treating vitamin A deficiency.

Nonivamide, glycol salicylate and levomenthol are topical analgesic/counterirritants acting via different sensory/anti-inflammatory mechanisms; niacin may provide vasodilation to improve local circulation—together they target shoulder musculoskeletal pain via complementary mechanisms.

Triamcinolone (corticosteroid) reduces inflammation/edema while framycetin (aminoglycoside antibiotic) treats the bacterial infection; together they address both infection and inflammation in otitis externa.

All three are antibiotics with different mechanisms, but this is not a recognized synergistic regimen for trachoma; colistin is unlikely to target intracellular Chlamydia and the combination may reflect empirical/broad-spectrum use or data ambiguity.
Both agents are calcium salts (calcium gluconate and calcium levulinate) that directly raise serum calcium to treat hypocalcemia, acting on the same therapeutic mechanism (calcium replacement).

Myrtecaine is a topical local anesthetic; salicylic acid is primarily a keratolytic/dermatologic agent rather than a proven analgesic for muscle pain. The combination’s mechanism for treating myalgia is unclear from these labels, so classification is uncertain.

Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects a β-lactam antibiotic from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against pathogens causing recurrent lower respiratory tract infections.

Nifuratel is antibacterial/antiprotozoal for vaginal infections; nystatin is an antifungal. Their combination likely addresses concurrent/mixed bacterial and yeast vaginitis rather than synergistic action on bacterial vaginosis.

Levodopa increases brain dopamine levels; piribedil is a dopamine receptor agonist (D2/D3). Together they enhance dopaminergic signaling in Parkinson disease via complementary mechanisms to improve symptomatic control.

Cyanocobalamin (B12) is the specific treatment for pernicious anemia; ferrous fumarate is an iron supplement used for iron-deficiency anemia. Their co-prescription likely reflects coexisting iron deficiency rather than a synergistic effect on the pathophysiology of pernicious anemia.
Noscapine is an antitussive (cough suppressant) and guaifenesin is an expectorant; they act via complementary mechanisms to reduce cough and promote mucus clearance in respiratory disorders.

Combination contains multiple antimicrobials with complementary mechanisms/spectra (sulfonamide phthalylsulfathiazole, nitrofuran furazolidone, luminal antiamoebic iodoquinol, aminoglycoside framycetin) plus kaolin as an adsorbent for symptomatic diarrhoea — combined to treat dysentery via antimicrobial and symptomatic pathways.

Guaiacol, eucalyptol (cineole) and camphor are used together for productive cough: guaiacol/eucalyptol act as expectorant/mucolytic and anti-inflammatory to enhance mucus clearance, while camphor provides topical counterirritant/airway soothing—complementary mechanisms targeting the same respiratory symptoms.

Lidocaine and procaine are local anesthetics (symptom/pain relief) while oxyquinoline is an antiseptic/antimicrobial; together they address both microbial cause and symptomatic pain of a skin lesion, complementary mechanisms for treating the condition.

Benzoic and salicylic acids are combined topically (e.g., Whitfield’s ointment) for dermatophytosis: benzoic acid has antifungal activity while salicylic acid is keratolytic/enhances penetration, producing complementary actions against the same infection.

Furazolidone is an anti‑infective for enteric pathogens and kaolin is an adsorbent that reduces diarrheal symptoms; framycetin is an antibiotic — together they act via complementary mechanisms to treat dysentery.

This is the established triple-combination for hyperpigmentation/freckles: hydroquinone inhibits melanin synthesis, tretinoin increases epidermal turnover and enhances hydroquinone penetration, and fluocinolone reduces inflammation/irritation—together enhancing depigmenting effect.

Ezetimibe inhibits intestinal cholesterol absorption (NPC1L1) while bempedoic acid inhibits ATP citrate lyase in hepatic cholesterol synthesis; complementary mechanisms that jointly lower LDL-C in familial hypercholesterolemia.

Both are topical antibiotics with complementary mechanisms (framycetin: aminoglycoside inhibiting protein synthesis; bacitracin: inhibiting cell wall synthesis) used together to broaden antimicrobial coverage against surgical wound infections.

Both are cytotoxic chemotherapies that damage tumor DNA by complementary mechanisms (trabectedin binds the minor groove and affects transcription/repair; doxorubicin intercalates and inhibits topoisomerase II), likely producing additive or synergistic antitumor effects in ovarian cancer.

Everolimus (mTOR inhibitor), basiliximab (IL-2R antagonist), and cyclosporine (calcineurin inhibitor) are complementary immunosuppressants targeting different T‑cell activation/proliferation pathways to prevent/treat renal transplant rejection.

Cetalkonium is an antiseptic; choline is a nutrient/excipient with unclear direct therapeutic action for oral ulcers. Insufficient evidence that the two act synergistically on ulcer pathology versus formulation/excipent use.

Cyclosporine (calcineurin inhibitor) and azathioprine (antimetabolite) are complementary immunosuppressants used together to prevent renal transplant rejection by inhibiting T-cell activation and proliferation via distinct pathways.

Framycetin is a topical antibiotic treating secondary bacterial infection; beclomethasone is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation. Combined use in atopic eczema addresses both infection and inflammatory symptoms, complementary mechanisms for the same condition.

All three are calcium salts that supply elemental calcium to correct calcium deficiency—same therapeutic mechanism (increase serum calcium), additive/synergistic effect on the single deficiency pathway.

Lidocaine provides local analgesia for hemorrhoid pain while glycerin acts as a topical emollient/rectal suppository to soften stool and reduce straining; together they address complementary mechanisms to treat hemorrhoid symptoms.
Tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects piperacillin from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against pathogens causing pelvic inflammatory disease.

All three are topical counterirritants/analgesics (methyl/menthyl salicylate, menthol, camphor) used together to provide local symptomatic relief of contusions via complementary cooling/warming and TRP channel–mediated analgesic effects.

Trypsin and bromelains are proteolytic enzymes that can promote fibrin degradation and reduce inflammation/edema; rutin has venotonic, anti-inflammatory and antithrombotic effects—together they act on complementary mechanisms relevant to thrombophlebitis.
Both agents are calcium salts that provide Ca2+ to bind fluoride and treat fluoride poisoning/hypocalcemia; they act on the same mechanism to strengthen calcium replacement/chelation.

condition_label: Malignant neoplasm of stomach stage IV
rationale_short: Tegafur+gimeracil+oteracil form S-1 (tegafur = 5-FU prodrug; gimeracil inhibits DPD to boost 5-FU; oteracil limits GI toxicity) combined with cisplatin (DNA crosslinker) provides complementary cytotoxic mechanisms and is a known synergistic regimen for advanced gastric cancer.

These agents are combined in topical rubefacient/analgesic formulations; methyl salicylate (counterirritant/NSAID-like), camphor and menthol (counterirritants/analgesics), and eucalyptus oil (mild analgesic/anti-inflammatory) act on complementary pathways to reduce pain and inflammation in contusions.

Benzydamine is a topical anti-inflammatory/analgesic for oral mucosa; cetylpyridinium is an antiseptic that reduces oral microbial burden. Together they address both inflammation/symptoms and microbial etiology of denture stomatitis.

Iodine and iodide are topical antiseptic agents with antimicrobial activity used for wound disinfection; combined use targets the same pathogenic microbes and enhances local antisepsis for traumatic wounds.

Topical heparin may promote hematoma resolution while levomenthol and glycol salicylate provide local analgesic/counterirritant effects; together they target complementary mechanisms relevant to contusion treatment.

Combination is of B vitamins (thiamine, FMN/riboflavin derivative, nicotinamide) typically used as nutritional/supportive therapy rather than documented synergistic antimicrobial action; indication 'Infections - pathogen unspecified' is vague and mechanism is unclear.
Both entries are calcium supplements that act to restore serum/bone calcium and support mineralization in osteomalacia, reinforcing the same therapeutic pathway.

Drugs include anti-inflammatory agents (dexamethasone, kebuzone/salicylamide derivatives), analgesics/local anesthetic (lidocaine, salicylamide derivative) and neurotrophic vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin), collectively targeting pain, inflammation, and nerve repair in neuritis.

Thyroid, porcine is thyroid hormone replacement for TSH deficiency; the other drugs are sex steroids/precursors used for hypogonadism. Central/isolated TSH deficiency often occurs with pituitary hormone deficiencies requiring multiple hormone replacements, indicating comorbid replacement rather than synergistic targeting of one pathway.

Tiotropium (LAMA) and salmeterol (LABA) provide complementary bronchodilation via muscarinic blockade and β2-agonism, while fluticasone (ICS) reduces airway inflammation—combined to improve bronchospasm control.

Both agents are antacids (magnesium trisilicate and algeldrate) that neutralize gastric acid and are used to relieve abdominal pain/indigestion; they act on the same mechanism to enhance symptom relief.

Ciclesonide (inhaled corticosteroid) reduces airway inflammation while tiotropium bromide (long-acting muscarinic antagonist) provides bronchodilation via muscarinic receptor blockade; complementary mechanisms address bronchospasm.

Acetylcysteine is a mucolytic that decreases mucus viscosity; tuaminoheptane is a topical vasoconstrictor/decongestant. Together they address complementary pathophysiologic features of sinusitis (mucus clearance and nasal congestion).

All four are topical counterirritants/analgesics (menthol, methyl salicylate, eucalyptus oil, camphor) that provide complementary cooling/warming and local analgesic effects for muscle strain, acting on related peripheral pain pathways.
Etodolac is an NSAID that reduces gout-related inflammation; acetaminophen provides additional central analgesia—together they enhance symptomatic pain control in gout via complementary mechanisms.

Fluocinolone is a corticosteroid reducing mucosal inflammation; Clonazoline appears to be a topical decongestant/vasoconstrictor. Together they address sinusitis via complementary anti-inflammatory and decongestant mechanisms.

No clear mechanistic rationale linking 'pirfotekh' (uncertain identity) and stannous chloride to osteogenesis imperfecta treatment; neither is a recognized OI therapy and no obvious synergy or side‑effect mitigation is known. Ambiguous/likely erroneous indication entry.

Chlorphenamine (H1 antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated allergic responses while guaifenesin is an expectorant that aids mucus clearance—complementary actions on airway symptoms in allergic asthma, though antihistamines have limited asthma efficacy.

All four are topical analgesics/counterirritants used for rheumatic pain with complementary mechanisms (nonivamide TRPV1 agonist, methyl salicylate salicylate analgesic, camphor counterirritant, levomenthol/TRPM8 cooling) that produce additive analgesic effects.

Local anesthetics (bupivacaine, lidocaine) provide immediate analgesia while corticosteroids (methylprednisolone, triamcinolone) reduce inflammation and provide longer-term symptom relief in epicondylitis; combined for complementary therapeutic effects.

Maltose/polymaltose is used as a carrier/complexing agent with iron (e.g., iron–polymaltose/ferric complexes) to improve iron delivery and absorption for iron‑deficiency (hypochromic) anemia, so both act on the same therapeutic mechanism.
Ascorbic acid enhances intestinal absorption and bioavailability of elemental/non-heme iron, boosting iron therapy efficacy for hypochromic (iron‑deficiency) anemia.

Bupivacaine and lidocaine are local anesthetics used for neuropathic pain/symptom control, while triamcinolone and methylprednisolone are corticosteroids for inflammation/relapse treatment in MS; the drugs address different symptomatic/comorbid issues rather than a shared disease-modifying mechanism.

Escin has venotonic, anti-edema and anti-inflammatory effects that can promote hematoma resolution; salicylic acid (a salicylate) provides anti-inflammatory properties—together they likely act on complementary inflammation/edema pathways to reduce hematoma. Role of topical vs systemic salicylate and bleeding risk is unclear.

Aspirin and acetaminophen provide antipyretic/analgesic effects via different mechanisms and ascorbic acid is used as supportive immune/nutritional therapy—combined to alleviate influenza symptoms rather than treat a comorbidity or mitigate side effects.

Acetaminophen and carbaspirin calcium are antipyretic/analgesics used to treat influenza symptoms (fever, pain); caffeine is known to potentiate analgesic efficacy and enhance symptom relief, indicating a synergistic symptomatic treatment mechanism.

drug_labels: ['Influenza A Virus A/California/122/2022 SAN-022 (H3N2) antigen (formaldehyde inactivated)', 'Influenza A Virus A/California/122/2022 SAN-022 (H3N2) antigen (formaldehyde inactivated)']
rationale_short: Both entries are the same influenza vaccine antigen; represents immunization boosting the same immune pathway against influenza (direct therapeutic/preventive mechanism), not comorbidity or side‑effect mitigation.

Ambiguous pairing: CHEBI:18248 is iron; CHEBI:34674 is dextran sulfate (not standard dextran used in iron-dextran therapeutics). Could represent an iron-dextran complex for iron deficiency, but labels are inconsistent—insufficient clear mechanistic or clinical indication. Recommend human review.
Perindopril (an ACE inhibitor) and amlodipine (a calcium channel blocker) act via complementary mechanisms to lower blood pressure and are commonly combined for additive antihypertensive effect.

Perindopril (ACE inhibitor) and indapamide (thiazide-like diuretic) act via complementary antihypertensive mechanisms (RAAS inhibition and diuresis/vascular effects) producing enhanced blood-pressure lowering.

Their co-use likely reflects co-occurring cardiovascular risk management rather than a targeted, synergistic treatment for high‑risk pregnancy.
Carisoprodol is a CNS muscle relaxant and aspirin is an NSAID/antiplatelet; neither drug targets acute myeloid leukemia mechanisms. Combination is not a recognized AML therapeutic strategy.

Potassium citrate and citric acid (both citrate sources) act as alkali providers/metabolize to bicarbonate, directly correcting acid–base disturbance in chronic metabolic acidosis—shared, complementary mechanism.

Sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor) plus valsartan (angiotensin receptor blocker) combine as an ARNI to enhance natriuretic peptides while blocking RAAS, producing complementary mechanisms that improve outcomes in heart failure.
Canagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) and metformin (reduces hepatic glucose production/improves insulin sensitivity) have complementary, nonredundant mechanisms to lower blood glucose in type 2 diabetes.

condition_label: lissencephaly type 1 due to doublecortin gene mutation

Fluocinolone is a topical corticosteroid that reduces local inflammation; ketocaine is a topical local anesthetic providing symptomatic pain/itch relief—complementary mechanisms addressing the same anorectal disorder.

Monopotassium phosphate and sodium bicarbonate are inorganic salts/pH/electrolyte agents with no clear joint mechanistic targeting of the specified protein; indication mapping to a UniProt entry is ambiguous. Insufficient evidence to call synergistic, comorbidity-driven, or side-effect relief.

Hydrocortisone (topical corticosteroid) and pramocaine (topical local anesthetic) are symptomatic/palliative agents for inflammation and pain; neither is an anticancer agent nor clearly reduces adverse effects of the other, so no clear mechanistic synergy or side-effect-relief relationship for anal canal adenocarcinoma.

Ox bile extract and pancrelipase are digestive enzyme/bile supplements and graphite is not a known therapy for adrenal (adrenocortical) insufficiency; combination does not target adrenal mechanisms and likely reflects misannotation or non-mechanistic association.

The combination’s mechanistic rationale for treating canker sores is unclear and may reflect misannotation or off-label use.

Netupitant (NK1 antagonist), palonosetron (5-HT3 antagonist) and dexamethasone (corticosteroid) target complementary pathways involved in chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting and are used together to enhance prophylactic efficacy.

Clavulanic acid is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects amoxicillin from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy in respiratory infections (acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis).

Drugs act on complementary mechanisms for cough: dextromethorphan is a central antitussive, pseudoephedrine is a nasal decongestant reducing postnasal drip, and promethazine is an antihistamine/antitussive reducing allergic contributors—together targeting multiple pathways for cough relief.

Balsam of Peru is a known contact allergen/fragrance, benzyl benzoate is an antiparasitic/solvent, and zinc oxide is a topical skin protectant; there is no clear mechanistic synergy for treating proctitis and the combination is ambiguous/atypical for this condition.

Dextran sulfate (a sulfated polysaccharide with anticoagulant/experimental uses) and D-glucose (metabolic substrate) have different, nonoverlapping actions; no clear evidence they target the same circulatory mechanisms or that one relieves the other's side effects. Relationship is ambiguous and likely formulation/unclear.

Cyanocobalamin (B12) and ferrous fumarate (iron) address different nutrient-dependent pathways of erythropoiesis; co-administration treats/contributes to anemia from multiple deficiencies and enhances overall hematologic response.
Thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant and nimesulide is an NSAID/analgesic; together they address muscle spasm and inflammation/pain in spinal conditions via complementary mechanisms.

Rhubarb (herbal, primarily laxative/enteric effects) and salicylic acid (topical keratolytic/anti-inflammatory) are not standard or clearly complementary treatments for oropharyngitis; no clear synergistic mechanism or side-effect mitigation identified. Evidence is insufficient/ambiguous.
Pheniramine (antihistamine) and tetryzoline (topical α-agonist vasoconstrictor) act on complementary mechanisms (histamine-mediated inflammation and mucosal vasodilation) to relieve nasal congestion.

Fluorometholone is an ophthalmic corticosteroid reducing inflammation; tetryzoline is an ocular vasoconstrictor that reduces conjunctival redness. They act on complementary pathways to treat blepharoconjunctivitis symptoms and inflammation.

Acetaminophen is an analgesic that can treat pain, but guaifenesin and phenylephrine target respiratory symptoms (expectorant, decongestant) and do not mechanistically treat abdominal pain; no clear synergistic mechanism for the indexed disease is evident.

Diosmin and hesperidin are venotonic/flavonoids used for chronic venous insufficiency and microcirculation; they are not established treatments for shock and do not mechanistically target shock pathways. The indication appears mismatched or ambiguous.

Amylmetacresol and dichlorobenzyl alcohol are topical antiseptics used in throat lozenges, not therapies for uterine inflammatory disease; no clear mechanistic synergy or comorbidity link—likely misannotation or insufficient evidence.

Terpin hydrate is an expectorant/mucolytic and chlorphenamine is an antihistamine; they act on complementary symptomatic mechanisms (mucus clearance and nasal histaminergic symptoms) to treat common cold.

Pholcodine (antitussive) and triprolidine (first‑generation antihistamine) provide complementary symptomatic treatment for common cold via different mechanisms (cough suppression and reduction of rhinorrhea/sneezing).

Acetaminophen is an analgesic for aches/pain; dextromethorphan (antitussive) and pseudoephedrine (decongestant) target cough/congestion—included for co-occurring cold/flu symptoms rather than synergistically treating generalized aches and pains.

All three are topical agents used to treat dermatitis with complementary mechanisms (coal tar: anti-inflammatory/keratoplastic; sulfur: keratolytic/antimicrobial; phenol: antiseptic/annesthetic), acting on multiple pathways to improve skin inflammation/symptoms.

Drugs address complementary symptoms/mechanisms of common cold: acetaminophen (antipyretic/analgesic), dextromethorphan (antitussive), promethazine (antihistamine/sedative/antiemetic), producing additive symptomatic relief.

Drugs have complementary mechanisms addressing multiple cold symptoms (phenylephrine: decongestant; brompheniramine: antihistamine reducing rhinorrhea/sneezing; dextromethorphan: antitussive), producing multi-symptom therapeutic synergy.

Both are antibacterials with complementary mechanisms: polymyxin B disrupts Gram-negative outer membranes enhancing uptake of intracellular-acting trimethoprim (DHFR inhibitor), so combined action can be mechanistically synergistic against bacterial infections.

Triamcinolone (corticosteroid) and kanamycin (aminoglycoside antibiotic) do not have a clear complementary mechanism for treating congenital macrodactyly of toes, which is typically a structural/overgrowth condition; combination appears unrelated or data artifact.

Prednisolone (corticosteroid) reduces ocular inflammation while ofloxacin (antibiotic) prevents/treats bacterial infection; commonly co‑used after cataract surgery to address complementary pathways (inflammation and infection) improving surgical outcomes.

Teferrol appears to be an iron supplement for iron deficiency anemia; icosapent (EPA ethyl ester) is an omega‑3 for lipid disorders and has no clear role in treating anemia or reducing iron therapy side effects. No clear mechanistic synergy or side‑effect relief; indication pairing is ambiguous.

Insufficient/ambiguous mechanistic information: peptide identity and rationale for combining with pyridoxine for abdominal pain are unclear; not clearly synergistic, nor evidently for side-effect relief or comorbidity.

Drugs are symptomatic therapies for pneumonia: acetaminophen (antipyretic/analgesic), dextromethorphan (antitussive) and promethazine (antihistamine/antiemetic/antitussive) act on complementary pathways to relieve symptoms rather than treating the infection itself.
Naproxen (NSAID) provides anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects while thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant; the two act on complementary pathways to reduce pain/stiffness in polymyalgia rheumatica.

Drugs target complementary symptomatic pathways of common cold: levocetirizine (antihistamine for rhinorrhea/sneezing), phenylephrine (nasal decongestant), ibuprofen (analgesic/antipyretic), dextromethorphan (antitussive), providing multi-symptom therapeutic synergy.

Acetaminophen provides analgesic/antipyretic effects, chlorphenamine reduces histamine-mediated nasal/sneezing symptoms, and caffeine potentiates analgesia and offsets antihistamine sedation — complementary symptomatic mechanisms for common cold.

Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is used for immune support/reducing cold duration while carbaspirin calcium (aspirin derivative) provides analgesic/antipyretic symptomatic relief; complementary mechanisms addressing the same disease symptoms.

Phenylephrine (decongestant), levocetirizine (antihistamine) and dexibuprofen (NSAID) target complementary symptom pathways in the common cold (congestion, rhinorrhea/sneezing, pain/fever), providing multi-modal symptomatic therapy.

Ascorbic acid may modulate immune response/duration of cold, while aspirin and acetaminophen provide complementary antipyretic/analgesic symptomatic relief via different mechanisms, jointly addressing cold symptoms and course.

Coal tar has keratoplastic/anti-inflammatory effects on scalp inflammatory disease; levomenthol provides topical antipruritic/cooling symptomatic relief. Together they act on complementary aspects of dissecting cellulitis rather than one mitigating the other's adverse effects.

Combination supplies multiple electrolytes and a buffer/infusate to restore fluid volume, serum osmolarity and electrolyte balance in hypotonic dehydration—acting together on the same corrective physiological mechanisms.

Chlorphenamine is an H1 antihistamine reducing histamine-mediated symptoms; cromolyn is a mast-cell stabilizer reducing mediator release. They act on complementary steps of the allergic response in seasonal allergic conjunctivitis.
Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects β-lactam antibiotics from enzymatic degradation, enhancing cefpodoxime’s antibacterial activity against pathogens causing acute URIs.

Paclitaxel (microtubule stabilizer) and cisplatin (DNA crosslinker) are complementary cytotoxic agents commonly combined in ovarian cancer to enhance tumor cell kill via distinct mechanisms; platinum sensitivity is particularly relevant in HRD-positive disease.

Brompheniramine (antihistamine) treats core allergic histamine-mediated symptoms while dextromethorphan (antitussive) and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) address concurrent symptoms; drugs act on different pathways to provide multi-symptom therapy for allergy.

Rituximab (anti‑CD20) plus cyclophosphamide (cytotoxic alkylator) are used together as chemoimmunotherapy for Richter transformation; hyaluronidase is an administration aid that facilitates subcutaneous delivery of rituximab rather than indicating a separate comorbidity or solely mitigating side effects.

Framycetin and polymyxin B are antibiotics targeting bacteria; hydrocortisone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation as an adjunct—they act on complementary mechanisms to treat bacterial infection.
Ibuprofen reduces pain/inflammation that can disrupt sleep, while diphenhydramine has sedative antihistaminic effects; they act on different pathways to improve difficulty sleeping.

Betamethasone is a corticosteroid (reduces inflammation) and Framycetin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic; combined in otic formulations to treat ear infections by addressing both infection and inflammation.

Ceftazidime is an antibiotic used for neutropenic infections; sodium carbonate is an antacid/buffering agent not known to have synergistic antimicrobial or disease-modifying effects for neutropenic enterocolitis. Relationship unclear and could be supportive/symptomatic or a data artifact.

Alpelisib (PI3Kα inhibitor) and fulvestrant (ER degrader) are mechanistically complementary in HR+ breast cancer, but alpelisib’s benefit depends on PIK3CA mutation. For a PIK3CA‑negative condition the combo lacks the established synergistic mechanism; classification is uncertain and warrants human review.
Dabrafenib (BRAF inhibitor) and Trametinib (MEK inhibitor) jointly inhibit the MAPK pathway; commonly combined to produce synergistic anti-tumor effects and delay resistance in BRAF-driven disease.

Fluoxetine (SSRI) and olanzapine (atypical antipsychotic) are used together (e.g., Symbyax) to augment antidepressant effects; they act on complementary neurotransmitter systems (serotonin reuptake inhibition plus dopamine/serotonin receptor antagonism) to improve depressive symptoms.

Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF angiogenesis inhibitor) combined with carboplatin (platinum DNA-damaging agent) and gemcitabine (nucleoside analogue cytotoxin) uses complementary mechanisms (anti-angiogenesis plus cytotoxicity) to enhance anti-tumor effect in liver cancer.

Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) targets angiogenesis while gemcitabine (antimetabolite) and carboplatin (platinum cytotoxic) provide complementary cytotoxic mechanisms against ovarian cancer, a multimodal, synergistic therapeutic approach.

Carfilzomib (proteasome inhibitor) and dexamethasone (corticosteroid) are used together for multiple myeloma, neither is an antihypertensive and both can worsen blood pressure; they do not mechanistically target resistant hypertension or relieve each other’s side effects.

drug_labels: ['Recombinant stabilized RSV A prefusion F antigen', 'Recombinant stabilized RSV A prefusion F antigen']
rationale_short: The listed product is an RSV prefusion F antigen (vaccine component) unrelated to ectopic pregnancy; duplicate entries suggest a data error rather than a mechanistic, comorbidity, or side‑effect relationship.

Macitentan (endothelin receptor antagonist) and tadalafil (PDE5 inhibitor) are primarily used for pulmonary hypertension; there is no clear, established synergistic anti-tumor mechanism for ependymoma linking these agents. Indication appears uncertain or off-label, so classification is ambiguous.

Clotrimazole is an antifungal for vaginal mycosis; the identity/mechanism of 'Evoclin (TN)' (CHEBI:3746) is unclear from provided data (could be another antifungal, antiseptic, or different agent), so mechanistic relationship is ambiguous.

Both agents are ergot alkaloids with no clear, established complementary mechanism for treating idiopathic cardiomyopathy; not clearly synergistic or used to mitigate each other’s side effects and indication appears atypical—needs verification.

Chlorhexidine (topical antiseptic) and lidocaine (local anesthetic) provide symptomatic antimicrobial and analgesic effects for pharyngeal cancer care, not synergistic anti-tumor action nor one drug relieving side effects of the other; does not reflect comorbidity-driven pairing.

Ampicillin is a β-lactam antibiotic and sulbactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects ampicillin from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against β-lactamase–producing pathogens in community-acquired pneumonia.

Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects amoxicillin from enzymatic degradation, expanding/strengthening its antibacterial activity against pathogens causing community-acquired pneumonia.

Clotrimazole is an antifungal treating the skin infection; dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation/itching. They act on complementary pathways to manage the same disease.

Conjugated estrogens + medroxyprogesterone are typically combined for HRT with complementary mechanisms, but the indexed condition is Nonoxynol-9 (a spermicide), a mismatch making the indication ambiguous.

Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy) plus paclitaxel (cytotoxic chemotherapy) are used together in breast cancer (notably PD-L1+ TNBC); chemotherapy can increase tumor antigen release and immunogenicity, complementing immune checkpoint blockade.

Sorbitol is an osmotic laxative increasing water content; docusate is a stool softener lowering surface tension—complementary mechanisms to relieve constipation.

Pepsin provides proteolytic activity dependent on gastric acidity; glutamic acid can act as an acidifying amino acid/stimulant of gastric secretions. Together they address low gastric acidity and impaired digestion in hypochlorhydria, representing complementary mechanisms.

Naphazoline (topical vasoconstrictor) reduces mucosal swelling, betamethasone (steroid) reduces inflammation, and tetracycline (antibiotic) treats infection—complementary actions addressing inflammation/infection and obstruction in acquired dacryostenosis.
Framycetin is an antibiotic targeting the bacterial cause; hydrocortisone is a topical steroid reducing inflammation—they act on complementary pathways to treat bacterial blepharitis.

Docetaxel is cytotoxic chemotherapy; prednisone provides anti-inflammatory/anti-androgenic and palliative effects and is given concomitantly to improve outcomes in prostate cancer—complementary mechanisms against the disease.

Hyaluronidase is an excipient enzyme used to enable subcutaneous delivery/absorption of rituximab rather than acting on lymphoma biology or primarily mitigating rituximab adverse effects; not a mechanistic synergy nor comorbidity.

Cyclizine is an antivertigo/antiemetic used for vertiginous symptoms of endolymphatic hydrops; pyridoxine is vitamin B6 and not a recognized synergistic therapy for this disease. The combination’s rationale (supplemental use, unclear synergy, or region-specific practice) is ambiguous.

All three drugs are sulfonamide antibiotics (inhibit bacterial folate synthesis) targeting the same antibacterial pathway for a bacterial ear infection, suggesting a shared mechanistic effect to enhance antimicrobial activity.

Dexamethasone (anti-inflammatory), chloramphenicol (antibacterial), and tetryzoline (vasoconstrictor for redness) act on complementary mechanisms— inflammation, infection, and symptomatic redness—addressing the same condition (eye irritation).

Both framycetin and bacitracin are topical antibiotics aimed at treating skin infections/inflammation; combined use likely targets the same disease mechanism (bacterial control) to broaden coverage or enhance antimicrobial effect in acne inversa (hidradenitis suppurativa).

Chlorphenamine (H1 antihistamine) and phenylephrine (alpha-1 vasoconstrictor/decongestant) act on complementary pathways to relieve allergic respiratory symptoms (reduce histamine-mediated symptoms and nasal congestion).

Erythromycin targets Cutibacterium acnes to reduce bacterial load/inflammation while isotretinoin reduces sebum production and follicular occlusion; together they act on complementary acne pathways.

Ibuprofen is an NSAID providing analgesia/anti-inflammatory effects for back pain, while glucosamine and chondroitin are supplements aimed at supporting joint/cartilage health; together they target pain via complementary mechanisms.

Ergotamine (vasoconstrictor/5-HT agonist) aborts migraine attacks, acetaminophen provides analgesia, caffeine enhances analgesic effect/absorption, and mecloxamine (antihistamine/antiemetic) addresses associated symptoms—complementary mechanisms targeting migraine pathophysiology.

Buprenorphine is the opioid partial agonist treating opioid dependence; naloxone is included to deter misuse/abuse and mitigate adverse effects of buprenorphine administration rather than provide synergistic therapeutic action.

Estradiol provides estrogen replacement; medroxyprogesterone (a progestin) is co-prescribed to prevent estrogen-induced endometrial hyperplasia/bleeding and reduce cancer risk, i.e., it mitigates an adverse effect of estrogen therapy.

Perflutren is an ultrasound contrast agent and plasma protein fraction is a volume expander; neither has a clear mechanistic role treating marginal ulcers. The pairing likely reflects unrelated uses (imaging/resuscitation) or data artifact, so mechanism unclear.

Cyanocobalamin (B12), thiamine (B1) and pyridoxine (B6) are nutritional supplements/supportive therapies for deficiency or treatment-related sequelae, not established direct therapies for tongue cancer; likely given for co-occurring malnutrition/deficiency rather than as anti-cancer mechanistic synergy.

Motixafortide (CXCR4 antagonist) plus filgrastim (G-CSF) are used together to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells for autologous transplant in multiple myeloma; they act via complementary mechanisms to enhance stem cell mobilization.

Corifollitropin alfa is an FSH analog that stimulates follicular development, while ganirelix, cetrorelix and degarelix are GnRH antagonists that prevent premature LH surge/ovulation; together they act on complementary reproductive endocrine pathways to enable controlled ovarian stimulation.

Cyproterone is a progestin/anti-androgen and estradiol is an estrogen; their combined role in ovarian cancer is not a clear mechanistic synergy and estradiol may stimulate ER+ tumors. Evidence for a purposeful complementary mechanism or side-effect mitigation is lacking in this context.

All three agents are antibiotics/antiprotozoals not known as treatments for small intestine adenocarcinoma; their use likely reflects management of co-occurring GI infections or decontamination rather than a unified anticancer mechanism.

Kanamycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic treating the bacterial infection; triamcinolone is a corticosteroid reducing intraocular inflammation. They act on complementary pathways to treat purulent endophthalmitis.

Nivolumab (PD-1 inhibitor) plus ipilimumab (CTLA-4 inhibitor) are dual immune checkpoint inhibitors that act on complementary pathways to enhance antitumor immune response in malignant pleural mesothelioma.

Infliximab (anti-TNF biologic) plus methotrexate (DMARD) are co-prescribed in RA because they target complementary inflammatory mechanisms and methotrexate reduces immunogenicity to infliximab, enhancing efficacy.
Clavulanic acid is a beta-lactamase inhibitor used with a beta-lactam antibiotic to protect the antibiotic from enzymatic degradation and enhance antibacterial efficacy against bacterial infections.
Both agents are topical antimicrobials/antiseptics used to reduce oral pathogens; combined use likely provides additive/ complementary antimicrobial effects against oral infection.

Dextromethorphan is a centrally acting antitussive, while phenylephrine (decongestant) and brompheniramine (antihistamine) reduce nasal congestion and postnasal drip; together they target multiple pathways contributing to cough.

Boric acid is an antiseptic and zinc oxide a skin protectant, but balsam of Peru is primarily an allergen and algeldrate is an antacid; the combination is heterogeneous and does not clearly represent mechanistic synergy or a side-effect relief or comorbidity-driven pairing.

Hydrocortisone provides anti-inflammatory effect, heparin offers local antithrombotic/anti-inflammatory activity for thrombosed hemorrhoids, and benzocaine gives local analgesia—complementary mechanisms addressing hemorrhoid pathology and symptoms.

Dequalinium is a topical antiseptic reducing oral microbial/infectious causes of glossitis; ascorbic acid (vitamin C) supports mucosal healing and corrects deficiency-related glossitis—complementary mechanisms addressing different contributors to the same condition.
Both drugs reduce gastric acidity by complementary mechanisms (sodium bicarbonate neutralizes existing acid; rabeprazole inhibits acid secretion), jointly promoting ulcer healing.

Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid reducing immune/inflammatory response; chlorphenamine is an antihistamine blocking histamine-mediated symptoms. Both act on complementary inflammatory pathways relevant to phlyctenulosis, augmenting therapeutic effect.

Estradiol dienanthate (estrogen) plus algestone acetophenide (progestin) are components of combined hormonal contraceptives and are not established treatments for ectopic pregnancy; no clear mechanistic synergy for treating ectopic pregnancy—likely annotation error or insufficient evidence.

Levonorgestrel + ethinylestradiol are combined hormonal contraceptives that prevent pregnancy via ovulation suppression and cervical changes, but they are not therapies for established ectopic pregnancy; the indication appears incorrect or ambiguous.

Coal tar has anti-proliferative/anti-inflammatory effects in psoriasis; salicylic acid is a keratolytic that removes scales and enhances topical penetration, so combined they act complementarily to improve efficacy.

Flupentixol (typical antipsychotic with antidepressant effects) combined with melitracen (tricyclic antidepressant) targets complementary neurotransmitter systems to enhance antidepressant efficacy; marketed as a fixed-dose antidepressant combination.

Salicylic acid is a keratolytic that removes scales and enhances topical penetration; flumethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation. Together they act on complementary mechanisms to improve psoriasis treatment.

Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) targets angiogenesis while carboplatin and gemcitabine are cytotoxic chemotherapies with distinct DNA-damaging/antiproliferative mechanisms; combined use provides complementary, potentially synergistic antitumor effects in recurrent primary liver cancer.

Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) plus carboplatin (platinum DNA crosslinker) and paclitaxel (microtubule inhibitor) target complementary tumor survival pathways (angiogenesis and cytotoxicity), a common multimodal, synergistic approach for recurrent primary liver cancer.

Drugs provide complementary mechanisms for common cold: expectorants (terpin hydrate, guaifenesin) to loosen mucus, antitussive (dextromethorphan) to suppress cough, and antihistamine (brompheniramine) to reduce rhinorrhea — targeting multiple symptom pathways.

Ibuprofen is an analgesic for aches/pains; phenylephrine is a decongestant for nasal congestion. The combo addresses co-occurring symptoms (e.g., cold/flu), not a shared/synergistic analgesic mechanism.

Combination targets multiple concurrent symptomatic pathways for common cold: expectorant (guaifenesin), antihistamine (triprolidine), opioid antitussive (codeine), and decongestant (pseudoephedrine), providing complementary symptomatic relief.
Topical framycetin is an antibiotic addressing secondary bacterial infection while flumethasone is a corticosteroid reducing inflammation; they act on complementary mechanisms to treat dermatitis.

Acetaminophen (central analgesic) plus etodolac (NSAID with peripheral anti-inflammatory/analgesic action) provide complementary analgesic mechanisms for symptomatic relief in rheumatoid arthritis, producing additive/synergistic pain control.

Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects the β-lactam antibiotic ceftibuten from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy against pathogens causing recurrent lower respiratory tract infections.

Triamcinolone is a corticosteroid that reduces local inflammation; framycetin is a topical antibiotic treating/preventing infection. Combined use addresses inflammatory and infectious components of local perianal/skin issues, representing complementary mechanisms.

Flumethasone is a corticosteroid (anti-inflammatory); framycetin is a topical aminoglycoside antibiotic. Combined use addresses inflammation and concurrent/secondary bacterial infection in erythematosquamous dermatosis, complementary mechanisms for same condition.

Orotic acid has occasional links to hepatic metabolism but xanthine is not a recognized treatment for decreased liver function; no clear mechanistic synergy or side‑effect mitigation. Indication appears ambiguous and requires expert review.
Ascorbic acid supports immune function and may reduce cold duration; acetaminophen provides symptomatic relief (fever/pain). They act on different pathways to benefit the same disease (common cold).

Salicylic acid (keratolytic) plus octasulfur (antifungal/antimicrobial) and benzoic acid (antifungal/preservative) provide complementary topical antifungal and scale-removing actions that enhance treatment of tinea capitis.

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine) relieves histamine-mediated nasal symptoms while ibuprofen (NSAID) provides analgesic/antipyretic and anti-inflammatory effects—complementary actions on different symptomatic pathways in acute URI.

Ceftolozane is a cephalosporin antibiotic and tazobactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor; together they enhance antibacterial activity against β-lactamase-producing pathogens causing hospital-acquired pneumonia.

Osimertinib is an EGFR-targeted TKI and pemetrexed is an antifolate cytotoxic chemotherapy; they act on distinct but complementary pathways to treat non-small cell lung carcinoma, providing additive/synergistic anti-tumor effects.

Rituximab (anti-CD20) with cyclophosphamide (alkylating agent) and fludarabine (purine analogue) comprise chemoimmunotherapy acting on complementary mechanisms against transformed CLL (Richter syndrome); hyaluronidase is an excipient to facilitate subcutaneous administration.
Amlodipine (calcium channel blocker) and candesartan (ARB) lower blood pressure via complementary mechanisms; commonly combined for enhanced antihypertensive effect.
Codeine (antitussive), acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) target different symptomatic mechanisms of the common cold, providing complementary symptomatic relief.

Pertuzumab and trastuzumab deruxtecan are anti-HER2 cancer therapies; they are not treatments for high-risk pregnancy. The association appears erroneous or out-of-scope for mechanism-based categories and needs clinical review.

Imipenem is the antibiotic; relebactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that restores/improves imipenem activity against resistant bacteria; cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase I preventing imipenem degradation and reducing nephrotoxicity. Together they enhance antibacterial efficacy for pneumonia.
Piretanide (diuretic) and ramipril (ACE inhibitor) are cardiovascular agents not known to target neural mechanisms of disinhibition; the indication pairing is incongruent or unclear in mechanism.

Sulbactam+durlobactam are beta‑lactamase inhibitor partners used to restore activity against resistant Gram‑negative bacteria (e.g., Acinetobacter); Chlamydia pneumoniae is an intracellular organism not typically treated with beta‑lactams, so the pairing does not reflect a clear mechanistic synergy for this disease.

Ibrutinib (BTK inhibitor) and rituximab (anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody) are combined in B‑cell malignancies to target complementary pathways—B‑cell receptor signaling blockade plus antibody‑mediated B‑cell depletion—producing enhanced clinical activity.

All three are ergot-derived constituents typically combined (ergoloid mixture) with similar vasoactive/ergot mechanisms—likely acting on the same pathway when used together; the specific relevance to idiopathic cardiomyopathy is unclear.

Dopamine is an inotrope/vasopressor used in acute heart failure; D‑glucose (dextrose) is an energy substrate/IV fluid not a heart‑failure–targeted agent. There is no clear mechanistic synergy or side‑effect mitigation; the combination is likely supportive/administrative or context-specific, so classification is ambiguous.

Cetuximab (EGFR monoclonal antibody) and fluorouracil (antimetabolite chemotherapy) act via complementary anti-tumor mechanisms and are commonly combined with platinum-based regimens to enhance cancer cell killing.

Pembrolizumab (anti‑PD‑1) and enfortumab vedotin (Nectin‑4 ADC) target complementary antitumor mechanisms—immune checkpoint blockade plus direct ADC cytotoxicity—used together in urothelial carcinoma to enhance efficacy.

Atorvastatin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) and aspirin (COX inhibitor/antiplatelet) have distinct anticancer mechanisms (mevalonate pathway inhibition, anti-inflammatory/antimetastatic effects) that could complement each other against tumor growth; specific evidence in carcinosarcoma is limited.

Prednisolone caproate is a corticosteroid reducing local inflammation to promote healing; cinchocaine is a topical local anesthetic providing pain relief. They act via complementary mechanisms addressing the pathology and symptoms of anal fissure.

Multiple antibiotics (chloramphenicol, rolitetracycline, colistin) provide broad antibacterial activity against eyelid pathogens while betamethasone reduces local inflammation—complementary mechanisms addressing infection and inflammatory component of bacterial blepharitis.

Valine, leucine and isoleucine are branched-chain amino acids given together to correct amino acid imbalances and influence neurotransmitter/metabolic pathways implicated in encephalopathy; mechanism plausible though specific evidence for uremic encephalopathy is limited.

Drugs act on complementary symptom pathways for atopic (allergic) rhinitis: brompheniramine (H1 antihistamine) and phenylephrine (decongestant) directly treat rhinitis symptoms; guaifenesin aids mucus clearance and hydrocodone suppresses cough—combined symptomatic, multi-mechanism therapy.

Colistin and framycetin are topical antibiotics that target the bacterial pathogen; hydrocortisone is a corticosteroid that reduces local inflammation and symptoms—adjunct drugs acting on complementary pathways against the same disease.

Methylprednisolone and triamcinolone are corticosteroids that can treat immune-mediated thrombocytopenia, but bupivacaine and lidocaine are local anesthetics with no clear role in treating thrombocytopenia; the combination’s intent is unclear and not clearly synergistic or for side-effect relief.

Topical hydrocortisone (anti‑inflammatory) plus lidocaine (local anesthetic for symptomatic relief), zinc oxide (barrier/protectant) and aluminum subacetate (astringent/drying) act on complementary mechanisms to treat pruritus ani.

Cefoperazone is a beta-lactam antibiotic and sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor; sulbactam protects cefoperazone from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy against beta-lactamase–producing bacteria.

Estradiol provides menopausal symptom relief; nomegestrol acetate (a progestin) is typically added to prevent estrogen-induced endometrial hyperplasia (reducing a key adverse effect) while supporting HRT.
Simeprevir (NS3/4A protease inhibitor), peginterferon alfa-2a (immune modulator) and ribavirin (nucleoside antiviral) are combined to target HCV via complementary antiviral mechanisms for genotype 1.

Clobetasone butyrate is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation; tetryzoline is an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor reducing redness. They act on different pathways to relieve eye irritation symptoms.

Both are direct-acting antivirals for HCV with complementary targets (simeprevir: NS3/4A protease inhibitor; sofosbuvir: NS5B polymerase inhibitor) used together to increase antiviral efficacy for genotype 1 chronic HCV.

Both are topical skin protectants used in dermatitis: petrolatum provides occlusive emollient/barrier repair while zinc oxide adds a protective/astringent and mild antiseptic effect; combined they complementarily protect and soothe inflamed skin.
Fluticasone is an inhaled corticosteroid that reduces airway inflammation; salmeterol is a long-acting β2-agonist that provides bronchodilation. Their complementary mechanisms enhance asthma control.

Umeclidinium (LAMA) + Vilanterol (LABA) provide complementary bronchodilation via muscarinic antagonism and β2-agonism while Fluticasone (ICS) adds anti-inflammatory effect—distinct but complementary mechanisms improving asthma control.

Tenoxicam (NSAID) reduces inflammation via COX inhibition while thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant that relieves spasm/pain; together they target complementary pathways to reduce inflammation and muscle-related symptoms in myositis.

Xylometazoline is a topical nasal decongestant for respiratory symptoms; dexpanthenol is a mucosal healing/soothing agent that can mitigate irritation/drying from topical decongestants. Combination is symptomatic with one drug reducing local adverse effects of the other rather than synergistic antiviral action.

Terpineol and eucalyptol are monoterpenes used as inhaled expectorant/anti-inflammatory agents in respiratory conditions; they likely provide additive mucolytic/anti-inflammatory symptomatic effects in acute laryngitis.

ICS (fluticasone) reduces airway inflammation while LABA (vilanterol) and LAMA (umeclidinium) provide complementary bronchodilation via β2 agonism and muscarinic blockade — combined therapy targets multiple COPD pathophysiologic mechanisms.

Dimetindene is an H1 antihistamine reducing allergic/inflammatory responses; phenylephrine is an α1 agonist vasoconstrictor reducing nasal congestion — complementary mechanisms addressing chronic rhinosinusitis symptoms.

Enoxaparin (anticoagulant inhibiting factor Xa/IIa) plus aspirin (antiplatelet COX-1 inhibitor) act on complementary aspects of thrombosis to reduce clot formation in ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

Both drugs reduce gastric acidity by complementary mechanisms—sodium bicarbonate neutralizes existing acid for rapid symptom relief while esomeprazole (a PPI) suppresses acid secretion for sustained healing—jointly addressing the ulcer pathology.

Tyrothricin (topical antibacterial) and cetrimonium (antiseptic) target the infective cause of pharyngitis while lidocaine provides local anesthetic symptom relief; agents act complementarily to treat the same condition.

Chlorhexidine and cetylpyridinium are topical antiseptics that reduce microbial/denture plaque load (including Candida), while benzydamine provides local anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects; together they address both infection burden and mucosal inflammation in denture stomatitis.

Triclosan is an antimicrobial that reduces cariogenic biofilm; sodium fluoride promotes enamel remineralization and inhibits demineralization—complementary mechanisms acting together to prevent/treat dental caries.

Quizartinib (FLT3 inhibitor) and cytarabine (antimetabolite chemotherapy) target complementary AML mechanisms—targeted inhibition of FLT3-driven signaling plus cytotoxic killing—producing synergistic therapeutic effects in AML.
Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects ampicillin from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial efficacy for bite wound infections.

Topical analgesics with complementary mechanisms: menthol (cooling/TRPM8), nonivamide (capsaicinoid/TRPV1 desensitization), glycol salicylate (salicylate counterirritant/analgesic); vitamin E likely excipient for skin. Combined to relieve muscle stiffness via synergistic topical effects.

Acetylcysteine is a mucolytic/secretolytic reducing mucus viscosity; tuaminoheptane is a sympathomimetic nasal decongestant causing vasoconstriction. They target complementary symptoms/pathways of the common cold, enhancing symptomatic relief.
Topical antibiotic (framycetin) treats the bacterial infection while corticosteroid (flumethasone) reduces inflammation and symptoms in otitis externa; complementary mechanisms for same condition.

All four are topical analgesics/counterirritants used for muscle pain: camphor, menthol (levomenthol) and nonivamide act on TRP receptors producing cooling/heat and desensitization, while glycol salicylate provides salicylate analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects—complementary mechanisms for treating myalgia.

These agents are combined in topical formulations for myalgia and act via complementary mechanisms—menthol/camphor as counterirritants (sensory TRP modulation), methyl salicylate as a local salicylate analgesic/anti-inflammatory, and eucalyptus oil as a mild analgesic/penetration enhancer—producing enhanced local analgesia.

Acetaminophen is an antipyretic; ascorbic acid is a vitamin/supplement with limited/uncertain evidence for treating fever or enhancing antipyretic effect. No clear mechanistic synergy or clear side‑effect relief relationship.

Algeldrate and magnesium trisilicate are antacids and kaolin is an adsorbent; together they provide complementary symptomatic relief for abdominal/GI pain via acid neutralization and adsorption of irritants.

Levothyroxine provides thyroid hormone and suppresses TSH-driven gland growth; potassium iodide supplies iodide and can acutely reduce thyroid activity/size—complementary mechanisms reducing goiter.

Tyrothricin (topical antibiotic) and benzethonium chloride (topical antiseptic) both reduce microbial load in oral lesions; combined use likely provides additive/overlapping antimicrobial effects addressing the same disease mechanism in oral ulcers.

Diclofenac topical in a hyaluronic acid gel (approved formulation) treats actinic keratosis; hyaluronic acid serves as vehicle and enhances retention/penetration, supporting diclofenac's therapeutic effect.

Combination includes multiple topical antimicrobials/antiseptic (tyrothricin, framycetin, benzalkonium) targeting the microbial cause of denture stomatitis; benzocaine provides local analgesia but overall regimen is aimed at treating the infection, representing complementary mechanisms against the same disease.

The listed topical agents provide complementary wound-care actions (antiseptic/anti-inflammatory/drawing agent/astringent/barrier protection) that act on multiple concurrent mechanisms to promote healing of a traumatic wound.

Methylprednisolone is the active corticosteroid used to treat alopecia areata; lidocaine and bupivacaine are local anesthetics typically used to reduce pain of intralesional steroid injections rather than provide additional disease-modifying activity.
