Carmoterol (a β2-agonist bronchodilator) and tiotropium (a long-acting muscarinic antagonist) act on complementary pathways to produce additive bronchodilation, treating bronchospasm.

Triclosan is an antibacterial antiseptic and octasulfur (elemental sulfur) provides keratolytic, anti‑seborrheic and antimicrobial effects; together they act on complementary pathways relevant to acne.

Triamcinolone is an anti-inflammatory corticosteroid and kanamycin is an antibiotic; combined they target inflammation and bacterial components of acne pathogenesis, providing complementary mechanisms.

Pseudoephedrine (decongestant) and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) target complementary symptomatic pathways (vasoconstriction/decongestion and histamine-mediated rhinorrhea/allergy) to relieve sinusitis symptoms.

Riboflavin and thiamine are B‑vitamin supplements typically given for nutritional deficiencies or supportive care, not as targeted, synergistic therapies for functional gastric disease; likely co‑treatment for concurrent deficiency rather than disease‑specific mechanism.

Donepezil (AChE inhibitor) and memantine (NMDA antagonist) provide complementary symptomatic mechanisms for Alzheimer disease; idebenone adds antioxidant/mitochondrial neuroprotective effects, so the drugs target multiple complementary pathways relevant to AD.
Piperacillin (beta-lactam antibiotic) combined with tazobactam (beta-lactamase inhibitor) preserves/enhances piperacillin activity against beta-lactamase–producing bacteria in abdominal infections.
Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor given with cefpodoxime to restore/enhance antibacterial activity against β-lactamase–producing pathogens in respiratory infections.

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine) plus pseudoephedrine (decongestant) act via complementary mechanisms to relieve different symptoms of hay fever (allergic rhinitis), producing additive symptomatic benefit.

Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects ticarcillin from enzymatic degradation, restoring/enhancing its antibacterial activity against infections—complementary mechanisms targeting same disease.
Unclear identity/therapeutic role of 'Isopto cetamide'; cannot determine whether it synergizes with betamethasone for keratoconjunctivitis or serves as supportive/preservative therapy.

Clenbuterol is a β2-adrenergic bronchodilator and ambroxol is a mucolytic/expectorant; together they target complementary pathophysiologic mechanisms (bronchoconstriction and mucus retention) in chronic lung disease.

Combination is a standard antacid/alginate formulation: algeldrate and calcium carbonate neutralize gastric acid, alginic acid forms a protective raft to prevent reflux, and dimethicone reduces gas/foam—complementary mechanisms treating heartburn.

Both agents are topical antiseptics with complementary antimicrobial actions (isopropanol causes protein/lipid denaturation; iodine causes halogenation/oxidation), used together to reduce pathogens for infection control.

Combination comprises direct-acting antivirals (paritaprevir NS3/4A protease inhibitor, ombitasvir NS5A inhibitor, dasabuvir NS5B inhibitor) plus ribavirin and ritonavir (pharmacokinetic booster), acting on multiple viral targets to clear HCV that causes cirrhosis.

Ciprofloxacin (fluoroquinolone) and piperacillin (anti‑pseudomonal β‑lactam) are antibiotics with complementary mechanisms/spectra commonly combined empirically to broaden coverage in febrile neutropenia.

Pseudoephedrine (decongestant), triprolidine (antihistamine) and guaifenesin (expectorant) target different symptoms/pathways of the common cold (nasal congestion, histamine-mediated rhinorrhea/sneezing, and mucus clearance), providing complementary therapeutic effects for the same condition.
Both agents are oral calcium supplements that increase systemic calcium availability and bone mineralization, acting on the same pathway to treat osteomalacia.

Cyanocobalamin (B12) and folic acid directly correct deficiencies that cause impaired DNA synthesis in macrocytic anemia; nicotinamide and thiamine are additional B‑vitamins commonly given as supportive supplementation, so the combination acts on the disease mechanism.

Cinnarizine suppresses vestibular/cochlear signals (antihistamine/calcium channel effects) while domperidone is a peripheral D2 antagonist antiemetic; together they target complementary pathways causing motion sickness.

Silver offers topical antimicrobial activity while salicylic acid provides keratolytic/comedolytic effects; together they target complementary acne pathogenic mechanisms (bacterial load and follicular occlusion).

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine), phenylephrine (decongestant) and acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) target different symptomatic/pathophysiologic aspects of sinusitis (allergic/inflammatory response, nasal congestion, and pain/fever), providing complementary effects for the same disease.

Carbidopa is a peripheral DOPA decarboxylase inhibitor given with levodopa to reduce peripheral conversion and side effects (nausea) and increase CNS levodopa availability, thereby supporting levodopa therapy for Parkinson disease.

Diclofenac is an NSAID reducing inflammation via COX inhibition; lidocaine provides local analgesia by blocking sodium channels. Together they target complementary pain/inflammation mechanisms for rheumatism.

Pipenzolate is an antimuscarinic antispasmodic that reduces GI motility peripherally; chlordiazepoxide is a benzodiazepine anxiolytic/central muscle relaxant that can reduce anxiety-driven or centrally-mediated gut hypermotility—distinct mechanisms that together target the same condition.

Ceftolozane is a beta-lactam antibiotic and tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor; tazobactam protects ceftolozane from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against UTI pathogens.

Both agents (Tyrothricin, Nitrofural) are topical antibacterial nitrofuran/peptide antibiotics; Trichomonas vaginalis is a protozoan treated with nitroimidazoles. No clear mechanistic synergy for treating trichomoniasis; could reflect topical/bacterial coinfection but that is speculative.

Electrolytes (Ca2+, K+, Na+, Mg2+), sodium bicarbonate and dextrose are used together to correct electrolyte and acid–base disturbances in chronic kidney disease, acting on related physiological pathways to manage CKD complications rather than treating an unrelated comorbidity.

Combination includes acetaminophen (antipyretic/analgesic), chlorphenamine (antihistamine) and phenylephrine (decongestant) which target different symptom pathways of influenza for combined symptomatic relief.

All three are symptomatic treatments for influenza acting on different but complementary pathways (NSAID: anti-inflammatory/analgesic, antihistamine: reduces rhinorrhea, decongestant: vasoconstriction to relieve congestion) to collectively relieve disease symptoms.

Salicylic acid is a keratolytic that enhances penetration and efficacy of topical corticosteroids like mometasone for hyperkeratotic skin conditions; the disease label (EXCESS LMW-DNA) is atypical for these agents, so human review recommended.

Dextromethorphan is an active agent for pseudobulbar affect and is clinically paired with a quinidine-type CYP2D6 inhibitor to increase plasma levels; CHEBI entry is quinine (not quinidine), so mapping is ambiguous but the combo suggests pharmacokinetic synergy.
Thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant addressing spasm-related pain; dexketoprofen is an NSAID reducing inflammation and nociceptive pain—complementary mechanisms for post‑traumatic pain.

Lurasidone (atypical antipsychotic) and valproic acid (mood stabilizer) are used together in bipolar depression; they act on complementary neurochemical targets to enhance mood-stabilizing/antidepressant effects.

Ascorbic acid enhances intestinal absorption and bioavailability of oral ferrous iron (reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+ and forms soluble complexes), increasing efficacy of iron supplementation for iron deficiency.
Bendroflumethiazide (thiazide diuretic) and nadolol (beta-blocker) have complementary antihypertensive mechanisms—reducing plasma volume and cardiac output/renin—providing additive BP lowering.

Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic reducing plasma volume; candesartan is an ARB blocking RAAS-mediated vasoconstriction. They act on complementary blood-pressure–lowering pathways and are commonly combined to improve hypertension control.

Corticosteroids (triamcinolone, methylprednisolone) provide anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive therapy for SJS while local anesthetics (bupivacaine, lidocaine) provide topical/analgesic symptom control; together they address complementary therapeutic mechanisms for the same condition.

Both are antacids used to neutralize gastric acid; magnesium salts tend to cause diarrhea while aluminum compounds (algeldrate) cause constipation, and the combination is commonly used to balance GI side effects while treating heartburn.
Algeldrate, kaolin, and magnesium trisilicate are antacids/adsorbents that act to neutralize gastric acid or adsorb irritants, jointly addressing the same mechanism causing heartburn.
Piperonyl butoxide is a metabolic synergist that inhibits insect P450s and enhances the insecticidal activity of pyrethrins against lice, so the two act together on the same target disease mechanism.

Cedazuridine is a cytidine deaminase inhibitor that prevents first-pass degradation of decitabine, increasing its bioavailability and thereby enhancing decitabine's hypomethylating therapeutic effect in chronic monocytic leukemia.

Glycol salicylate (topical salicylate analgesic/anti-inflammatory) plus menthol and camphor (counterirritant analgesics) are combined to enhance topical pain relief for low back pain; vitamin E likely a skin protectant/excipient but does not change the intent of combined analgesic mechanisms.

Both agents supply citrate anions that are metabolized to bicarbonate, providing systemic alkalinization to counter lactic acidosis; potassium citrate also supplies K+ while citric acid contributes citrate substrate—cooperative acid–base buffering effect.
Vonoprazan (acid suppressant) raises gastric pH and enhances antibiotic stability/efficacy; combined with amoxicillin this improves bacterial eradication (e.g., H. pylori).

Topical salicylate esters (ethyl, glycol, methyl salicylate) provide local analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects while methyl nicotinate acts as a vasodilator/rubefacient to increase local blood flow and enhance topical effect—complementary mechanisms for treating low back pain.

Tegafur is a prodrug of 5-FU; co-administered uracil inhibits dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase-mediated 5-FU catabolism, increasing 5-FU exposure and antitumor activity (UFT regimen) in colorectal cancer.

Aspirin is an NSAID that relieves dysmenorrhea via prostaglandin inhibition. Ascorbic acid is a vitamin/supplement with limited or inconsistent evidence for dysmenorrhea and does not clearly provide mechanistic synergy or mitigate aspirin adverse effects. Insufficient clear mechanistic rationale.

Terpineol and eucalyptol are monoterpenes with overlapping mucolytic, decongestant and anti-inflammatory properties used to relieve nasal congestion in rhinitis, so combined action likely enhances symptomatic effect.
Bisacodyl (stimulant laxative) increases colonic motility while docusate (stool softener) reduces stool hardness; complementary mechanisms enhance efficacy for treating constipation.
Both agents can produce laxative/effervescent/osmotic effects in the gut; combined use would act on GI motility/stool consistency to relieve constipation.

Dexpanthenol promotes tissue repair, DMSO provides anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects and enhances penetration, and heparin reduces local inflammation/edema—together they target inflammation and healing at the enthesis.

Clidinium is an anticholinergic antispasmodic reducing GI cramping while chlordiazepoxide is an anxiolytic/sedative; together they address complementary symptomatic pathways in colitis rather than one drug treating adverse effects of the other.

Cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase I to prevent imipenem degradation and nephrotoxic metabolite formation, reducing renal toxicity and enhancing imipenem efficacy for infections in neutropenic patients.

Hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide diuretic) plus losartan (ARB) lower blood pressure via complementary mechanisms (diuresis and RAS blockade), jointly reducing stroke risk—therapeutic synergy for the same disease pathway.

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated rhinorrhea/sneezing while pseudoephedrine (alpha-adrenergic decongestant) produces vasoconstriction to relieve nasal congestion; complementary mechanisms targeting the same condition.

Triprolidine (antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated symptoms while pseudoephedrine (sympathomimetic decongestant) causes nasal vasoconstriction; complementary mechanisms both relieve nasal congestion.

Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) has general antioxidant/immune effects; identity and mechanism of 'Menglytate' (UNII:C3B9R0E116) are unclear. Insufficient information to determine mechanistic synergy, side-effect relief, or comorbidity-driven use for throat irritation.
Tyrothricin is a topical antimicrobial targeting the infection; benzocaine is a local anesthetic providing symptomatic (pain) relief rather than enhancing antimicrobial effect.
Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects β-lactam antibiotics from enzymatic degradation, enhancing cefdinir's activity against β-lactamase–producing bacteria causing tonsillitis.

Dexlansoprazole (PPI) reduces gastric acid to promote mucosal healing; domperidone is a prokinetic that enhances gastric emptying and esophageal clearance, complementing acid suppression to reduce reflux and support healing of erosive esophagitis.

Phenylpropanolamine (vasoconstrictor) and chlorphenamine (H1 antagonist) act on different pathways to reduce nasal congestion; acetaminophen and dextromethorphan address other cold symptoms but the regimen targets multiple concurrent mechanisms to relieve respiratory symptoms.

Levocetirizine (antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated rhinorrhea/itching while pseudoephedrine (sympathomimetic) produces nasal vasoconstriction/decongestion; complementary mechanisms treating the same symptom.

These substances are the constituent electrolytes and buffer of lactated Ringer’s/Hartmann-type IV fluids; combined they restore intravascular volume, electrolytes and acid–base balance to treat fluid loss.

Both drugs are antibiotics with different mechanisms (oxytetracycline: protein synthesis inhibitor; polymyxin B: membrane disruptor) and can be combined to broaden/strengthen antibacterial activity for a localized (focal) infection.

Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) increases intestinal calcium absorption; the calcium salts provide substrate for bone mineralization. Combined they act on complementary pathways to improve bone density in osteoporosis.

Sofosbuvir (NS5B polymerase inhibitor) and ribavirin (broad antiviral nucleoside analog) are combined to enhance antiviral activity against HCV and improve sustained virologic response rates in genotype 2 via complementary mechanisms.

Mepyramine (H1 antihistamine) blocks histamine-mediated itching/vasodilation while hydrocortisone (corticosteroid) suppresses inflammation and immune-mediated components; complementary mechanisms commonly used together to treat urticaria.

Conjugated estrogens treat/prevent osteoporosis; medroxyprogesterone is added mainly to prevent estrogen-induced endometrial hyperplasia rather than directly treating bone loss, i.e., it mitigates an adverse effect of estrogen while enabling osteoporosis therapy.

All three are topical barrier/emollient agents used to protect and soothe sensitive skin: zinc oxide provides a physical protective/soothing effect while mineral oil and dimethicone act as occlusive emollients to restore/maintain the skin barrier, producing complementary effects for the same condition.

Amphotericin B (membrane-disrupting fungicidal) plus flucytosine (antimetabolite inhibiting nucleic acid synthesis) are standard induction therapy for systemic cryptococcosis and act synergistically on different fungal targets.

Bacitracin (topical antibiotic) and dequalinium (antiseptic) both act against bacteria causing impetigo, providing overlapping antibacterial effects; diphenylpyraline is an antihistamine for symptoms but does not negate the antimicrobial synergy.

Tetracycline and sulfamethizole are antibiotics targeting bacterial causes of cystitis; phenazopyridine is an adjunctive urinary analgesic providing symptomatic relief—together they address infection plus symptoms, constituting complementary/adjunctive therapeutic mechanisms for cystitis.

Glucosamine and chondroitin are used together to support cartilage matrix and reduce joint breakdown, while dimethyl sulfone (MSM) has anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects; combined they target complementary pathways in knee osteoarthritis.
Algeldrate and magnesium trisilicate are antacids that neutralize gastric acid; levomenthol has antispasmodic/analgesic properties—together they address multiple mechanisms causing abdominal colic.

Abacavir, lamivudine, and zidovudine are nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors combined as ART for HIV to increase antiviral efficacy and reduce resistance by jointly inhibiting reverse transcriptase.

Salicylic acid and lactic acid are keratolytics that remove hyperkeratotic tissue in heloma (corns); polidocanol adds local anesthetic/symptom relief/sclerosing activity. Together they target the lesion and symptoms via complementary mechanisms.

Econazole is an antifungal addressing common fungal etiology of intertrigo; triamcinolone is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation and pruritus—together treating both infection and inflammatory symptoms.

Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor paired with a β-lactam antibiotic (the listed cephalosporin/penicillin-like compound) to restore/enhance antibacterial activity for acute cystitis — complementary mechanisms against same infection.
Ledipasvir (NS5A inhibitor) plus sofosbuvir (NS5B polymerase inhibitor) are complementary direct-acting antivirals used together to treat HCV by inhibiting distinct steps in viral replication.

Pyridoxine (B6) is the direct treatment for pyridoxine-deficiency anemia; co-administered B vitamins (B12, B1 derivative, pantothenic acid) and vitamin E support hematopoiesis and related metabolic pathways, providing complementary effects on the same disease mechanism.

Alginic acid (alginate) forms a floating barrier/raft to prevent reflux while dimethicone acts as an anti-foaming agent reducing surface tension and aiding raft formation; complementary mechanisms that jointly relieve heartburn.

Belladonna (anticholinergic) can reduce GI spasms and secretions while aluminium salt functions as an antacid to neutralize gastric acid; together they act on complementary mechanisms relevant to heartburn symptoms.

Magnesium trisilicate and algeldrate are antacids for heartburn; dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent added to reduce gas/bloating and other GI side effects of antacid therapy rather than provide separate mechanistic synergy.

Diclofenac is an NSAID providing analgesia/anti-inflammatory effects; thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant/antispasmodic reducing muscle-related pain—complementary mechanisms addressing post-operative pain.

Pyridoxine and pyridoxal phosphate are forms of vitamin B6; pyridoxine is converted to the active cofactor PLP which directly restores B6-dependent heme synthesis, so both act on the same disease mechanism (vitamin B6 deficiency).

Etodolac is an NSAID providing anti-inflammatory analgesia; thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant reducing post-op muscle spasm–related pain. They act on complementary pathways to relieve postoperative pain.

Drugs act via complementary mechanisms to treat flatulence: dimethicone (anti-foaming reduces gas bubbles), pancrelipase (improves digestion to reduce gas production from malabsorption), and bromopride (prokinetic increases GI motility to aid gas transit).

Topical corticosteroid (fluprednidene acetate) reduces inflammation/immune response in eczema while miconazole treats the fungal infection; together they address inflammation and underlying infection in infected eczema.

Both hypromellose and dextran sulfate are viscosity-enhancing/lubricating agents used in artificial tear formulations to improve tear film stability and ocular surface lubrication for dry eye; they act together on the same therapeutic mechanism.

Thalidomide (immunomodulatory/anti-angiogenic), melphalan (alkylating cytotoxic), and prednisone (corticosteroid) have complementary mechanisms and are used together (MPT regimen) to treat multiple myeloma, indicating mechanistic synergy.

Povidone and hydroxyethylene are polymeric lubricants/viscosity agents used in artificial tears that both act to stabilize/replace the tear film and lubricate the ocular surface, jointly addressing dry eye pathophysiology.
Cyanocobalamin (B12) and folic acid act in the same one-carbon/DNA synthesis pathways and together can correct megaloblastic anemia and support hematopoiesis in B12-related deficiency.

Sulfogaiacol is a guaiacol derivative expectorant used to relieve cough; citric acid is commonly used in cough formulations to acidify/aid mucosal secretions and formulation performance — both appear to act to relieve cough and could be complementary.
Sulfogaiacol is a mucolytic/expectorant reducing mucus viscosity while dextromethorphan is a central antitussive; they act on complementary mechanisms to relieve cough.

Combination includes antitussives (pentoxyverine, diphenhydramine) plus expectorant/mucolytic agents (guaifenesin, sulfogaiacol) that act on complementary mechanisms to reduce cough and clear secretions.

Dextromethorphan is an antitussive, phenylephrine is a nasal decongestant, and thonzylamine is an antihistamine/anticholinergic; they act on complementary pathways to relieve cough and associated upper airway symptoms.

Dextromethorphan is an antitussive suppressing the cough reflex; phenylephrine is a vasoconstrictor/decongestant that reduces nasal congestion/postnasal drip which can provoke cough—combined to address complementary pathways causing cough.

Drugs address complementary mechanisms for cough: dextromethorphan is an antitussive (cough reflex suppression), ephedrine is a sympathomimetic decongestant/bronchodilator, and promethazine reduces histamine-mediated postnasal drip and has sedative/antitussive effects, producing synergistic symptomatic relief.
Dextromethorphan is a central antitussive and guaifenesin is an expectorant that thins/clears mucus; they act via complementary mechanisms to reduce cough symptoms.
Terbutaline (bronchodilator), Loratadine (antihistamine reducing allergic/postnasal triggers) and Noscapine (antitussive) act on complementary mechanisms to reduce cough symptomatology.

Codeine is a central antitussive while ephedrine provides decongestant/bronchodilator effects; citric acid can aid expectoration; thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant with unclear relevance—overall the drugs act via complementary mechanisms to relieve cough.

Betamethasone is an anti-inflammatory for noninfectious eyelid dermatoses; gentamicin is an antibiotic used to treat or prevent concurrent bacterial infection rather than acting on the primary noninfectious disease mechanism.

Agents act on complementary hemostatic mechanisms: rhThrombin promotes fibrin formation, Simoctocog alfa replaces deficient factor VIII, aprotinin reduces fibrinolysis, and calcium is a coagulation cofactor — together enhancing clotting to treat hemorrhagic disease.

Halcinonide is a topical corticosteroid (anti-inflammatory); salicylic acid is a keratolytic that removes scale and can enhance topical steroid penetration—complementary mechanisms for treating hyperkeratotic/noninfectious eyelid dermatoses.

Sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor) and ertugliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) act on complementary mechanisms (incretin enhancement and renal glucose excretion) to provide additive glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

Metformin, linagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor) and empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) have complementary glucose-lowering mechanisms addressing hepatic glucose production/insulin sensitivity, incretin-mediated insulin secretion, and renal glucose excretion for type 2 diabetes.

Metformin (improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic glucose production) combined with saxagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor increases incretin-mediated insulin secretion) target complementary glucose-lowering pathways in type 2 diabetes.

Topical framycetin (antibiotic) targets bacterial component of pustular acne while beclomethasone (corticosteroid) reduces inflammatory response—complementary mechanisms addressing infection and inflammation.

Both cetrimonium and benzalkonium are quaternary ammonium topical antiseptics/surfactants with antimicrobial activity; when combined in topical formulations for diaper rash they act on the same antimicrobial pathway to enhance microbial control.

All four are topical agents with complementary actions (anti-inflammatory/astringent/antiseptic and barrier-protective) that target multiple pathogenic aspects of atopic eczema, supporting a synergistic therapeutic effect.
Both amylmetacresol and dichlorobenzyl alcohol are topical antiseptics used together to reduce oral microbial load; combined antimicrobial actions target the pathogenic bacteria driving gingivitis.

Magnesium trisilicate and algeldrate are antacids that neutralize gastric acid; dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent that reduces gas and improves symptomatic relief. Together they address gastric ulcer symptoms via complementary mechanisms.

Calcium carbonate is an antacid used to neutralize gastric acid for ulcer symptom relief; dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent that reduces gas/foaming and belching often caused by antacid use, i.e., it mitigates side effects rather than independently treating the ulcer.

Diclofenac (NSAID) reduces inflammation via COX inhibition; lidocaine provides local analgesia via sodium channel blockade. Together they provide complementary pain/inflammation control for arthritis.

Sodium chloride directly corrects hyponatremia; mannitol is an osmotic agent primarily used for intracranial pressure and can alter serum osmolality but its concurrent use with saline for treating hyponatremia is not a clearly established, specific synergistic or side-effect–relief strategy. Clinical intent is ambiguous.

Difenoxin is an opioid antidiarrheal reducing intestinal motility; atropine is an anticholinergic that also decreases GI motility and is co-formulated (and discourages abuse). Together they act on complementary pathways to treat functional diarrhea.

Both agents are potassium salts (alkalinizing/potassium supplements) used to correct electrolyte/acid–base disturbances common in IBD rather than directly treating intestinal inflammation; combination addresses comorbidity/complication management.

Dihydrocodeine is a known antitussive; benzoic acid is typically a preservative/excipient and not clearly an active antitussive or side-effect mitigator for dry cough. Unclear if combination is therapeutic synergy or formulation artifact.

Simvastatin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis while ezetimibe inhibits intestinal cholesterol absorption (NPC1L1); combined use produces additive/ complementary LDL-C lowering in familial hypercholesterolemia.
Dextromethorphan is a central antitussive and diphenhydramine adds antihistaminic/anticholinergic drying and sedative effects; together they reduce cough via complementary mechanisms.

Rosuvastatin is a lipid-lowering statin treating familial hypercholesterolemia; aspirin is an antiplatelet used to reduce cardiovascular event risk rather than directly lowering cholesterol. Their combination addresses co-occurring cardiovascular risk, not a shared lipid-lowering mechanism.

Tetryzoline is an ocular vasoconstrictor that reduces redness; fluorometholone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation. Together they address complementary mechanisms of conjunctivitis (symptom relief and anti-inflammatory therapy).
Codeine is an antitussive for dry cough; amlodipine is an antihypertensive not known to treat cough—likely co-prescribed for a comorbid condition rather than a joint mechanism treating cough.

Sulfametrole (a sulfonamide) and trimethoprim inhibit successive steps in bacterial folate synthesis, producing a synergistic (potentiated) bactericidal effect used to treat bacterial infections like cellulitis.

Topical salicylic acid (keratolytic/anti-inflammatory), benzoic acid (antimicrobial/antifungal/preservative), and elemental sulfur (keratolytic/antiparasitic) target complementary skin mechanisms that can reduce pruritus, suggesting synergistic therapeutic effects.

Multi-symptom cold/flu combination: acetaminophen is an antipyretic for fever while guaifenesin (expectorant), ephedrine (decongestant), and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) provide complementary symptomatic relief via different mechanisms for the same illness.

Acetaminophen is the antipyretic addressing fever; phenylephrine (decongestant) and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) target nasal/allergic symptoms and potassium citrate is unrelated to fever. The combination does not appear to act synergistically on fever and is not clearly for side-effect relief or comorbidity.
Acetaminophen and salicylamide are both antipyretics and likely combined to enhance fever reduction; phenylephrine and clemizole address other concurrent cold symptoms in a multi-symptom formulation.
Caffeine has known analgesic adjuvant effects, but choline is not a well-established pain treatment; mechanistic synergy for pain is unclear and evidence for this combination in pain is insufficient.
Aspirin (NSAID/COX inhibitor) and oxycodone (opioid receptor agonist) act via distinct complementary mechanisms to provide additive/enhanced analgesia for pain.
Mestranol (estrogen) plus norethisterone (progestin) function as a combined hormonal therapy to suppress ovarian androgen production and raise SHBG, reducing free androgen effects in androgen excess.

Antazoline is an antihistamine that reduces histamine-mediated itching; tetryzoline is an alpha-adrenergic vasoconstrictor that reduces ocular redness/vasodilation. They act on complementary pathways to relieve ocular pruritus.
Ethinylestradiol + norelgestromin (combined hormonal contraceptive) suppress ovarian androgen production and increase SHBG, reducing free androgens and treating androgen excess.
Dimethicone is an anti-foaming/anti-flatulence agent and graphite (a carbon adsorbent) would act by sequestering gas/irritants—complementary mechanisms to relieve meteorism.

Glycerin is an osmotic agent used to acutely lower intraocular pressure; sodium chloride (hypertonic saline) is primarily used topically to reduce corneal edema and is not a standard IOP-lowering agent. The joint mechanism for treating ocular hypertension is unclear/ambiguous.

Elemental sulfur (octasulfur) is a topical antifungal/keratolytic; potassium carbonate can act as an alkaline keratolytic/pH modifier that may enhance sulfur solubility/penetration and combined antifungal/keratolytic effects for superficial mycoses.

Aspirin is an analgesic; sodium bicarbonate is an antacid/buffering agent commonly combined with aspirin (e.g., effervescent formulations) to neutralize gastric acid, reduce GI irritation and aid dissolution/absorption, thus primarily mitigating aspirin side effects.

Chlorhexidine and cetylpyridinium are topical antiseptics reducing microbial load; benzydamine is a local anti‑inflammatory/analgesic. They act on complementary mechanisms (antimicrobial + symptomatic/inflammatory relief) for pharyngitis.

Benzocaine is a topical local anesthetic for pain; diphenhydramine has antihistamine and local anesthetic/membrane-stabilizing effects and is used topically for symptomatic relief—together they provide complementary mechanisms to reduce pain.
Tizanidine is a muscle relaxant (central α2 agonist) and acetaminophen is an analgesic; they act via different mechanisms to reduce pain, providing additive/synergistic analgesia.

Mefenamic acid provides analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects while dicyclomine is an antispasmodic; combined they target pain and smooth muscle spasm to relieve gastrointestinal cramps via complementary mechanisms.

Clobetasol provides potent anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive effect for inflammatory alopecia, minoxidil stimulates hair growth via follicular vasodilation/K+ channel opening, and tretinoin can enhance topical penetration and follicular responsiveness—complementary mechanisms addressing hair loss.

Licorice has reported anti-androgen effects, but ammonium carbonate has no clear mechanistic role in treating androgen excess or mitigating licorice side effects. Insufficient evidence of synergy or intended side‑effect relief.

Levothyroxine is the standard replacement therapy for myxedema (hypothyroidism). Potassium iodide is typically used for hyperthyroidism or iodine prophylaxis and has no clear synergistic, comorbidity, or side‑effect relief role in treating myxedema—likely an unclear or erroneous pairing.
Both are topical lozenge antiseptic/analgesic agents used together for infective pharyngitis, providing complementary local antimicrobial and symptomatic relief against the same condition.

Both tetracaine and benzocaine are topical local anesthetics that block voltage-gated sodium channels to reduce pain/itch; combined use provides additive/enhanced topical analgesia for insect bites.

Antazoline is an antihistamine targeting allergic mechanisms; tetryzoline is a topical vasoconstrictor reducing ocular redness—complementary mechanisms addressing allergic conjunctivitis symptoms.

Topical combination addresses multiple complementary mechanisms for anal fissure: hydrocortisone reduces inflammation, cinchocaine provides local anesthesia/pain relief, framycetin offers topical antibacterial cover, and esculin may support wound/healing or anti-inflammatory effects—jointly targeting disease pathophysiology.

Tetryzoline is a topical decongestant (vasoconstrictor) reducing nasal congestion; betamethasone is a corticosteroid reducing mucosal inflammation—they act on complementary mechanisms to relieve sinusitis symptoms.

Hydrocortisone is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation; pramocaine is a local anesthetic relieving pain—complementary mechanisms treating anal fissure symptoms.

Polymyxin B is an antibacterial for ear discharge; lidocaine provides topical analgesia for symptoms rather than enhancing antimicrobial activity or reducing antibiotic adverse effects—combination is supportive/symptomatic, not mechanistic synergy or comorbidity.

Dexamethasone targets allergic inflammation, tetrizoline provides symptomatic vasoconstriction (reduces redness), and chloramphenicol covers/ prevents bacterial infection; together they address eye allergy through complementary mechanisms (anti-inflammatory, symptomatic relief, and infection control).

Calcium and cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) enhance intestinal calcium absorption and bone mineralization; phosphorus provides phosphate for hydroxyapatite formation—together directly support bone density in osteopenia.

Eucalyptus, lavender, and tea tree oils have reported antimicrobial/anti-inflammatory properties but there is insufficient evidence that topical or aromatherapy use treats deep bone infection (osteomyelitis) or that these agents provide a clear mechanistic synergy for this indication.

Phenylephrine is the active vasoconstrictor used to treat hemorrhoids; 'Hard fat' is an excipient/ointment or suppository base (vehicle) rather than a second therapeutic agent with synergistic mechanism.

Coal tar and pine tar have antiproliferative/anti-inflammatory/antipruritic effects for psoriasis; salicylic acid is a keratolytic that removes scale and enhances penetration/efficacy of tar preparations—complementary mechanisms for scalp psoriasis.

No clear evidence these two CNS depressants are used together to mechanistically treat ‘atypical behavior’; not a side-effect mitigation or comorbidity pairing. Combination is ambiguous and potentially unsafe rather than synergistic.

Topical antibiotics (Polymyxin B, Framycetin) plus corticosteroid (Dexamethasone) address concurrent infection and inflammation in the eye via complementary antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory mechanisms.

Econazole is an antifungal (targets the pathogen) and triamcinolone is a topical corticosteroid (reduces inflammation/symptoms); together they address pathogen burden and inflammatory symptoms of tinea corporis. However steroids can mask/worsen fungal infections, so this is borderline.

Clotrimazole is an antifungal that targets the dermatophyte causing tinea corporis while hydrocortisone is a topical corticosteroid that reduces inflammation/pruritus; they act via complementary mechanisms to improve the same condition.

Sodium fluoride promotes enamel remineralization and inhibits cariogenic bacteria, while sodium bicarbonate acts as a mild abrasive and pH buffer to neutralize acids and help remove plaque; complementary mechanisms that jointly reduce dental plaque/caries risk.

Calcium provides the mineral deficit; cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) enhances intestinal calcium absorption and homeostasis; phylloquinone (vitamin K1) supports bone mineralization and calcium utilization—complementary mechanisms addressing calcium deficiency.

Combination contains topical agents with complementary actions for hemorrhoids (zinc oxide = skin protectant/astringent, bismuth subgallate = astringent/hemostatic/odor control, levomenthol = local analgesic/cooling, calcium carbonate often used as mild antacid/adsorbent—collectively providing local protection, astringency, and symptom relief).

Citric acid provides citrate to chelate/alkalinize urine and inhibit calcium stone formation; magnesium (magnesite) can inhibit crystallization; gluconolactone (a source of gluconic acid) may contribute chelation/urinary chemistry modification — together they act on stone dissolution/prevention mechanisms.

Acetaminophen and an aspirin-like agent provide complementary analgesic/anti-inflammatory actions for musculoskeletal pain, while caffeine is a known analgesic adjuvant that potentiates pain relief—together producing synergistic analgesic effects.

Chlorphenamine is an antihistamine used to treat hay fever symptoms; acetaminophen is an analgesic/antipyretic addressing pain/fever rather than allergic mechanism. They address different symptomatic aspects rather than a shared mechanistic synergy or comorbidity.

Menthol and nonivamide are topical counterirritants (TRP modulators) providing analgesia; glycol salicylate supplies topical salicylate analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects; vitamin E offers antioxidant/tissue-repair support — complementary mechanisms addressing pain, inflammation, and healing in contusions.

Menthol, camphor and methyl salicylate are combined as topical counterirritant/analgesics that act via different but complementary mechanisms (cooling/TRPM8 activation, mild irritant/vasodilation, salicylate analgesia) to relieve pain from contusions.

Salicylic acid is a keratolytic and Myrtecaine is a topical anesthetic; neither has a clear synergistic mechanism for treating contusions and indication is atypical. Data ambiguous—clinical rationale unclear.

Betamethasone is an anti-inflammatory corticosteroid while colistin, chloramphenicol, and rolitetracycline are antibiotics; together they address both infection and inflammatory damage in keratoconjunctivitis.

All three agents are antimicrobials targeting gut bacteria; combined use likely aims to alter intestinal microbiota and reduce bacterial-driven inflammation in IBD, representing complementary antimicrobial mechanisms against dysbiosis.

Flupentixol is a typical antipsychotic for psychosis; melitracen is a tricyclic antidepressant. Their combination is typically to address comorbid depressive/anxiety symptoms rather than producing synergistic antipsychotic effects for schizophrenia.

Cetirizine (H1 antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated allergy symptoms while pseudoephedrine (adrenergic decongestant) relieves nasal congestion; they target complementary mechanisms for allergic respiratory disease.

All three agents are used to relieve GI symptoms: algeldrate and magnesium hydroxide act as antacids/acid-neutralizers (and affect motility), while dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent reducing gas; together they target multiple symptom mechanisms causing abdominal pain.
Fenoterol (β2 agonist) and ipratropium (antimuscarinic) provide additive bronchodilation via distinct mechanisms, commonly combined for acute severe asthma/status asthmaticus.

Multiple trace element supplements (zinc, manganese, selenium, potassium iodide, gluconates) jointly replace deficient micronutrients to correct trace element deficiency—complementary/reinforcing therapeutic mechanism.

Doravirine (NNRTI) combined with lamivudine and tenofovir (NRTIs) targets HIV reverse transcriptase via complementary mechanisms; standard combination antiretroviral therapy with synergistic antiviral effect and resistance prevention.

Hydrocortisone (topical steroid) reduces inflammation and promotes healing of the fissure while cinchocaine (local anesthetic) provides analgesia; combined they address complementary pathological features/symptoms of anal fissure to improve treatment.
Methylprednisolone reduces gout inflammation; lidocaine provides local analgesia—complementary mechanisms that jointly reduce pain and inflammation in gout.
Codeine is an antitussive (suppresses cough) and guaifenesin is an expectorant (loosens/thins mucus); complementary mechanisms addressing cough and mucus clearance for upper respiratory symptoms.

Betamethasone provides potent anti-inflammatory effect for conjunctival inflammation; naphazoline is a topical vasoconstrictor that reduces redness/symptoms; tetracycline offers antibacterial activity and anti-inflammatory/modulatory effects on ocular surface/eyelid disease. Together they target complementary pathways to reduce inflammation and symptoms of noninfective conjunctivitis.

Triamcinolone and methylprednisolone are corticosteroids addressing inflammatory/immunologic processes central to rheumatic myocarditis; lidocaine (antiarrhythmic) and bupivacaine (analgesic/local anesthetic) address cardiac arrhythmia and symptom control—a multimodal regimen targeting inflammation and cardiac manifestations of the same disease.

Enmetazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects cefepime from enzymatic degradation, restoring/enhancing cefepime’s antibacterial activity against beta-lactamase-producing pathogens in urinary tract infections.
Opioid (oxycodone) plus NSAIDs (naproxen, ibuprofen) and acetaminophen employ multimodal analgesia acting on different pain pathways to enhance analgesic effect and reduce required opioid dose.

Electrolytes (Ca2+, K+, Na+, Mg2+), sodium bicarbonate and dextrose are used together to correct electrolyte and acid–base disturbances in chronic kidney disease, acting on related physiological pathways to manage CKD complications rather than treating an unrelated comorbidity.

Combination addresses multiple influenza symptom mechanisms: acetaminophen (antipyretic/analgesic), dextromethorphan (antitussive), guaifenesin (expectorant), and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) acting on different pathways to relieve overall disease symptoms.

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine), acetaminophen (antipyretic/analgesic) and caffeine (analgesic adjuvant/stimulant) are combined to target multiple symptomatic pathways in influenza (histamine-mediated symptoms, fever/pain, and enhanced analgesia), providing complementary therapeutic effects.

Efgartigimod reduces pathogenic IgG (treats antibody-mediated autoimmunity); hyaluronidase is used to enable/enhance subcutaneous absorption of efgartigimod, increasing its exposure and therapeutic effect rather than acting as independent therapy.

Efgartigimod reduces pathogenic IgG (treats antibody-mediated autoimmunity); hyaluronidase is used to enable/enhance subcutaneous absorption of efgartigimod, increasing its exposure and therapeutic effect rather than acting as independent therapy.

Azilsartan (ARB) lowers angiotensin-II–mediated vasoconstriction and chlorthalidone (thiazide-like diuretic) reduces volume via natriuresis; together they provide complementary BP and volume control relevant to complications of inadequate hemodialysis rather than one drug treating side effects of the other.

Methimazole treats the underlying hyperthyroidism by inhibiting thyroid hormone synthesis; atenolol provides symptomatic control of adrenergic manifestations (tachycardia, tremor). Complementary mechanisms addressing the same disease (thyrotoxicosis).

Naproxen (NSAID) reduces inflammation and nociceptive pain while thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant that relieves spasms; together they target complementary mechanisms to reduce post‑traumatic pain.

These ingredients are combined in topical analgesic formulations: methyl salicylate (salicylate analgesic/anti-inflammatory) plus camphor and levomenthol (counterirritants/analgesics); chlorobutanol serves as preservative/antiseptic in the same topical formulation. Together they act via complementary local pain‑relief mechanisms for sprain.

Phenylephrine and guaifenesin are decongestant/expectorant agents used for upper respiratory symptoms; choline is a nutrient. This combination likely addresses co-occurring cold/sinus symptoms that accompany or cause headaches rather than a shared mechanistic, synergistic anti-headache effect.
Fosinopril (an ACE inhibitor) and hydrochlorothiazide (a thiazide diuretic) are complementary antihypertensives acting on different mechanisms to produce additive blood-pressure lowering.

Acetaminophen is the analgesic for headache while dextrmethorphan (antitussive), guaifenesin (expectorant) and chlorphenamine (antihistamine) target respiratory/cold symptoms; combination treats multi-symptom illness rather than synergistic headache mechanisms.

Acetaminophen and propyphenazone are analgesics with complementary mechanisms used to treat headache; ascorbic acid is likely adjunctive but the combination is aimed at enhanced analgesic/antipyretic effect.

Enalapril (ACE inhibitor) and hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide diuretic) lower blood pressure via complementary mechanisms (RAAS inhibition + diuresis), producing additive antihypertensive effects; common combination for hypertension.

Hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide diuretic) and moexipril (ACE inhibitor) act on complementary BP-lowering mechanisms (volume reduction and RAAS/vascular tone), commonly combined for additive antihypertensive effect.
Ramipril (ACE inhibitor) and felodipine (dihydropyridine CCB) lower blood pressure via complementary mechanisms; commonly used together for additive antihypertensive effect.

Ramipril (ACE inhibitor) and hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide diuretic) target complementary blood-pressure mechanisms (RAAS inhibition and diuresis/volume reduction) and are commonly combined for additive antihypertensive effect.

Atenolol (beta-1 blocker) reduces heart rate/contractility while chlorthalidone (thiazide-like diuretic) lowers blood volume and vascular resistance; complementary mechanisms for treating hypertension.

Nitrendipine (dihydropyridine CCB) and enalapril (ACE inhibitor) act via complementary antihypertensive mechanisms on vascular smooth muscle calcium influx and renin-angiotensin system, respectively, providing additive BP-lowering effects.
Hydrocortisone (anti-inflammatory corticosteroid) and crotamiton (topical antipruritic) both treat pruritus via complementary mechanisms, likely providing additive symptomatic relief.

Both Tyrothricin (peptide antibiotic) and Dequalinium (quaternary ammonium antiseptic) are topical antimicrobials used in throat preparations to reduce bacterial load in tonsillitis, acting on complementary/overlapping antimicrobial mechanisms.

Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is appropriate for vitamin D deficiency; fluoride ion is not a treatment for this condition and is unrelated therapeutically—combination likely incidental or data artifact rather than synergistic or comorbidity-based.

Miconazole is an antifungal that reduces fungal burden; triamcinolone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation/itch in fungal skin infections. They act on complementary mechanisms to treat mycoses.

Etofenamate is an NSAID used for musculoskeletal pain/inflammation (appropriate for spondylosis); niacin is a lipid‑modifying vitamin not known to target degenerative spinal disease. Combination likely reflects treatment of coexisting conditions rather than a shared or synergistic mechanism for spondylosis.

Cholecalciferol corrects vitamin D deficiency and enhances intestinal calcium absorption; calcium carbonate provides substrate for bone mineralization — complementary actions on the same calcium/vitamin D pathway to treat deficiency.

Betamethasone provides anti-inflammatory steroid effect, naphazoline is a vasoconstrictor reducing conjunctival redness, and tetracycline offers antimicrobial and additional anti-inflammatory activity; together they address inflammation, vasodilation, and potential infection in atopic conjunctivitis.

Kanamycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic treating bacterial infection; triamcinolone is a corticosteroid reducing inflammation. Together they address infection and the inflammatory component of wound infections via complementary mechanisms.

Loperamide slows intestinal motility to reduce stool frequency; dimethicone reduces gas/foaming and abdominal discomfort. They target complementary symptom mechanisms to manage non-infective diarrhoea.

Both drugs are topical antibiotics with complementary mechanisms (aminoglycoside/protein synthesis inhibition and cell wall synthesis inhibition) that broaden coverage and enhance antibacterial effect against wound infections.

PPI (esomeprazole) reduces gastric acidity and enhances antibiotic efficacy; amoxicillin and rifabutin are complementary antibiotics targeting the same bacterial infection (e.g., H. pylori) — combined to improve eradication via complementary mechanisms.
Lipase, amylase and protease are pancreatic enzyme replacements that together restore digestive enzyme activity in exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, acting on the same disease mechanism.

Pheniramine is an H1-antihistamine reducing histamine-mediated itching/inflammation; naphazoline is an ocular alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor reducing redness—complementary mechanisms treating allergic (atopic) conjunctivitis.

condition_label: pneumonia caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rationale_short: Gentamicin (aminoglycoside) and carbenicillin (beta-lactam) have complementary antibacterial mechanisms; beta-lactam disrupts cell wall allowing enhanced aminoglycoside uptake, producing synergistic bactericidal activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Zofenopril (ACE inhibitor) and hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide diuretic) have complementary antihypertensive mechanisms and are commonly combined to produce additive/ synergistic blood-pressure lowering.

Combination targets multiple PMS symptom mechanisms: acetaminophen for pain, pamabrom as a diuretic for fluid retention, and mepyramine (antihistamine/sedative) for mood/sleep/irritability — complementary symptom-directed actions for premenstrual tension.

Lazertinib is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and amivantamab is a bispecific antibody targeting EGFR and MET; together they act on complementary/overlapping EGFR-driven pathways to overcome resistance and enhance antitumor activity in metastatic NSCLC.

Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF angiogenesis inhibitor) plus interferon alfa (immunomodulatory with anti-proliferative/anti-angiogenic effects) are used together in renal cell carcinoma to enhance anti-tumor activity via complementary mechanisms.

Sodium fluoride promotes remineralization/inhibits demineralization of dentin; sodium bicarbonate buffers oral acidity and aids cleaning, supporting remineralization and enhancing fluoride effectiveness against caries.

Thiamine (B1) directly treats decreased B1; pyridoxine (B6) is a different B vitamin and does not specifically correct B1 deficiency. Combination likely reflects multivitamin use or nutritional supplementation rather than a clear mechanistic synergy for B1 deficiency.
Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that can protect β-lactam antibiotics like ceftibuten from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against pathogens causing tonsillitis.

Loratadine (antihistamine) and pseudoephedrine (systemic decongestant) act via complementary mechanisms to reduce allergic nasal symptoms and vasoconstrict mucosa, enhancing relief of nasal congestion.

Paritaprevir, dasabuvir, ritonavir, and ombitasvir are direct-acting antivirals (and a PK booster) used to treat HCV; they do not mechanistically treat autoimmune primary biliary cholangitis. This appears to be a misannotation or outside expected mechanism.

Combination contains topical counterirritants/analgesics (levomenthol, nonivamide, glycol salicylate) plus vitamin E as emollient/antioxidant; agents act via complementary symptomatic mechanisms (analgesia, counterirritation, skin protection) to treat chilblains.

Tiotropium (long-acting muscarinic antagonist) and formoterol (long-acting β2-agonist) provide complementary bronchodilation via distinct receptors/pathways for bronchitis/COPD, producing additive/synergistic effect.

Chlorphenamine (H1 antihistamine) blocks histamine-mediated symptoms; triamcinolone (corticosteroid) reduces inflammation and immune mediator production—complementary mechanisms used together to control urticaria.

Thalidomide (an immunomodulatory/anti-angiogenic agent) combined with dexamethasone (a corticosteroid) is a standard regimen for multiple myeloma; the drugs have complementary mechanisms that enhance anti-myeloma cytotoxicity.
Folic acid corrects folate-dependent DNA synthesis and ferrous sulfate supplies iron for hemoglobin synthesis; both complementarily support erythropoiesis to treat anemia.
For chronic Q fever, hydroxychloroquine raises phagolysosomal pH which enhances doxycycline activity against Coxiella burnetii; combination is used for synergistic antimicrobial effect.
Cobicistat is a pharmacokinetic enhancer (CYP3A inhibitor) that boosts plasma levels and efficacy of the protease inhibitor atazanavir for treating HIV, acting to strengthen the antiviral effect.

Lopinavir is an HIV protease inhibitor and ritonavir is used primarily as a pharmacokinetic booster (CYP3A4 inhibitor) to raise lopinavir levels and enhance antiviral efficacy; both act to increase protease inhibition against HIV.

Zinc oxide is a topical barrier/antiseptic for skin irritation; cod liver oil is an oral source of vitamins A/D/omega-3s with possible skin-supporting effects. The combination for intertrigo is atypical and mechanistic synergy is unclear from available info.

Atorvastatin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis while ezetimibe blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption (NPC1L1); combined therapy provides complementary LDL-C lowering in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

Chloroxylenol is an antiseptic for infection prevention in skin wounds; benzocaine is a topical local anesthetic for pain relief; benzyl alcohol serves as a preservative/mild antiseptic/solvent. Together they address complementary mechanisms (antisepsis + analgesia) relevant to treating abrasions.
Ledipasvir (NS5A inhibitor) plus sofosbuvir (NS5B polymerase inhibitor) are complementary direct-acting antivirals used together to treat HCV by inhibiting distinct steps in viral replication.

Flumethasone is a topical corticosteroid that reduces inflammation; salicylic acid is a keratolytic/antiscaling agent. They target complementary pathogenic features of seborrheic dermatitis, enhancing overall efficacy.

Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine addressing allergic etiology; ammonium chloride acts as an expectorant to relieve cough. Ethanol and potassium citrate appear unrelated or as excipient/supportive agents, so two drugs target complementary mechanisms for allergic cough.

Naphazoline (vasoconstrictive decongestant) and diphenhydramine (antihistamine) act on complementary pathways reducing nasal/Eustachian tube congestion and allergic inflammation, jointly relieving symptoms and promoting middle-ear drainage in otitis media.

Hydrocortisone is a topical corticosteroid reducing inflammation in proctitis; cinchocaine is a topical local anesthetic providing analgesia. They act via complementary mechanisms to treat inflammation and pain of the same disease.

Relebactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that restores/improves imipenem activity; cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase preventing imipenem degradation. Both enhance imipenem’s antibacterial efficacy for pyelonephritis.

Pyridoxine (B6) is the direct treatment for pyridoxine-deficiency anemia; co-administered B vitamins (B12, B1 derivative, pantothenic acid) and vitamin E support hematopoiesis and related metabolic pathways, providing complementary effects on the same disease mechanism.

Ceftolozane is a beta-lactam antibiotic and tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects ceftolozane from enzymatic degradation; the approved combination enhances antibacterial activity for complicated UTIs including pyelonephritis.

Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is the specific treatment for pyridoxine deficiency anemia; thiamine (vitamin B1) treats a different deficiency. Co-administration likely reflects coexisting B‑vitamin deficiencies or general supplementation rather than a synergistic mechanism for this anemia.

Magnesium hydroxide and algeldrate are antacids that address dyspeptic/gastric contributors to gas-related symptoms, while atropine (an antimuscarinic) reduces GI spasms; together they act on complementary gastrointestinal mechanisms to relieve flatulence symptoms.
Cinitapride is a prokinetic that enhances GI motility; dimethicone is an anti-foaming agent that reduces gas bubbles. They act on complementary mechanisms to relieve flatulence.

Naproxen provides anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects (COX inhibition) while thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant that reduces spasms and associated pain; complementary mechanisms acting on post-operative pain.

Ixabepilone (microtubule-targeting epothilone) and capecitabine (oral prodrug of 5‑FU antimetabolite) have distinct complementary mechanisms and have been used together for metastatic breast cancer, providing additive/ synergistic antitumor effects.

rationale_short: Combination includes inactivated poliovirus antigens (types 1, 2, 3) that together provide multivalent immunity against poliomyelitis; other listed antigens are co-formulated vaccine components for other pathogens.

Both agents target HER2 in breast cancer: pertuzumab blocks HER2 dimerization while trastuzumab deruxtecan is an anti-HER2 antibody–drug conjugate delivering cytotoxic payload, providing complementary mechanisms against the same pathway.

Hydroxyethyl (likely a viscous lubricant/tear substitute) improves tear film retention and lubrication, while dexpanthenol promotes epithelial healing and moisture—complementary mechanisms addressing tear deficiency and surface repair in dry eye.

Codeine is an opioid antitussive (suppresses cough reflex), guaifenesin is an expectorant (loosens/thins mucus), and phenyltoloxamine is an H1 antihistamine (reduces allergic/postnasal secretions); together they target complementary mechanisms to relieve cough.
Bromhexine and sulfogaiacol are both expectorant/mucolytic agents used to treat cough by enhancing mucus clearance; they act on the same therapeutic mechanism to improve expectoration.

Dextromethorphan (antitussive), guaifenesin (expectorant), chlorphenamine (antihistamine) and phenylpropanolamine (decongestant) act on complementary mechanisms to relieve cough and associated symptoms.

Dextromethorphan is an antitussive, phenylpropanolamine a decongestant (reducing postnasal drip), and chlorphenamine an antihistamine; together they target multiple mechanisms causing cough and so act synergistically to relieve the symptom.
Diphenhydramine (antihistamine/antitussive) reduces cough reflex; bromhexine is a mucolytic and guaifenesin is an expectorant—together they act on complementary mechanisms to relieve cough.
Terbutaline is a bronchodilator reducing bronchospasm while guaifenesin is an expectorant that loosens mucus; they act on complementary mechanisms to improve cough.

Combination uses complementary mechanisms for cough: dextromethorphan is an antitussive, guaifenesin is an expectorant (thins/loosens mucus), and pseudoephedrine is a nasal decongestant—together addressing multiple pathways of cough and related symptoms.

Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation; diphenhydramine is an H1-antihistamine that relieves histamine-mediated itching/allergic symptoms—complementary mechanisms addressing eyelid dermatoses.

Metformin, linagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor) and empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) have complementary glucose-lowering mechanisms addressing hepatic glucose production/insulin sensitivity, incretin-mediated insulin secretion, and renal glucose excretion for type 2 diabetes.

Trimethoprim and polymyxin B are combined topical antibiotics with complementary mechanisms (DHFR inhibition and membrane disruption) to broaden spectrum and enhance antibacterial effect in blepharoconjunctivitis.
Both drugs are chelating agents (dimercaprol and EDTA) used to treat lead poisoning; they act on the same disease mechanism (metal chelation/removal) and can be used together to enhance lead removal.

Petrolatum (emollient/occlusive) and zinc oxide (physical barrier/skin protectant/antiseptic) act complementarily to protect and heal irritated skin in diaper rash, enhancing barrier and soothing effects.

Zinc oxide is a topical barrier/skin protectant for diaper rash; talc absorbs moisture and reduces friction. Together they address complementary mechanisms (barrier protection + moisture control) for the same condition.

Combination of topical barrier/emollient agents (petrolatum, zinc oxide, lanolin) with a counterirritant/antipruritic (levomenthol) provides complementary protective, emollient, and sensory antipruritic effects for pruritus ani.
All three are topical barrier/emollient/protectant agents (occlusive emollients and protective oxide) that complementarily restore skin barrier and reduce transepidermal water loss in atopic eczema.

Octasulfur (elemental sulfur) has known topical antiparasitic/keratolytic activity for skin parasites; potassium carbonate is not a recognized antiparasitic and likely serves as an excipient/pH modifier. Mechanistic relationship for treating parasitic skin disease is unclear from provided data.

Nifuratel and nystatin are used together for vulvovaginal candidiasis; both have antifungal activity (different/ complementary antimicrobial spectra), so combined therapy likely enhances antifungal effect against Candida.

Algeldrate (aluminum hydroxide) and magnesium hydroxide neutralize gastric acid together (complementary antacid action); dimethicone reduces gas and mannitol serves as excipient/laxative adjunct—overall a combined antacid formulation acting synergistically to relieve gastric-ulcer symptoms.
These electrolytes and glucose are combined as intravenous rehydration/crystalloid solutions to restore isotonic fluid and electrolyte balance; components act together to correct dehydration.
Glucosamine is used for symptomatic/joint support in arthritis while lidocaine provides local analgesia; they act via complementary mechanisms to reduce symptoms of the same disease (arthritis).

Clioquinol is an antimicrobial that can treat underlying infectious/inflammatory causes of pigment changes; hydrocortisone is an anti-inflammatory steroid that reduces inflammation-driven hyperpigmentation. Together they address concurrent pathways contributing to skin hyperpigmentation.

Gentamicin is an antibiotic targeting the bacterial cause of cellulitis; fluocinolone is a corticosteroid reducing inflammation. They act on complementary mechanisms (antimicrobial + anti-inflammatory) to address the disease manifestations.

condition_label: Haemophilus influenzae secondary bacterial infection of acute bronchitis
rationale_short: Framycetin is an antibacterial addressing H. influenzae; dexamethasone is an anti-inflammatory reducing airway inflammation—complementary mechanisms addressing infection and symptomatic inflammation in bacterial acute bronchitis.

Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic reducing microbial/irritant load; lidocaine is a topical anaesthetic providing symptomatic relief of throat pain/cough. They act via complementary mechanisms to treat hoarse voice.

Acetaminophen and salicylamide are both antipyretics/analgesics providing additive fever-reducing effects; chlorphenamine adds symptomatic relief for allergic/cold symptoms but supports overall symptomatic treatment of fever/viral illness.
Both potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate alkalinize urine and increase urinary citrate, reducing calcium stone formation—acting on the same preventive pathway for nephrolithiasis.

Citric acid (citrate) and magnesium both reduce kidney stone formation by chelating calcium/oxalate and altering urinary chemistry; gluconolactone (gluconic acid precursor) may contribute acidifying/chelating effects—combined actions target stone formation mechanisms.
Aspirin provides antipyretic effect; caffeine can potentiate analgesic efficacy and codeine adds opioid analgesia—together they enhance symptomatic relief of fever-associated pain/symptoms.
Ephedrine (sympathomimetic decongestant/bronchodilator) and guaifenesin (expectorant) act on different mechanisms to relieve cough symptoms, providing complementary symptomatic relief.

Acetaminophen (central antipyretic) and dexibuprofen (COX inhibition) both reduce fever via complementary mechanisms; caffeine commonly potentiates analgesic/antipyretic effects as an adjuvant, producing additive/synergistic effect against fever.
Aspirin is an analgesic/anti-inflammatory (COX inhibitor) while meprobamate provides sedation/muscle relaxation (GABAergic), complementary mechanisms that can jointly reduce pain symptoms.

Zinc oxide (a topical skin protectant) and diphenhydramine (an antihistamine) do not have clear complementary analgesic mechanisms for treating pain; no evidence of synergistic pain-targeting or one ameliorating the other's side effects. Combination use appears context-dependent and ambiguous.

Etynodiol (progestin) plus ethinylestradiol (estrogen) are combined oral contraceptives used to treat androgen excess by complementary mechanisms: suppressing ovarian androgen production and increasing SHBG to lower free androgens.

Corticosteroids (triamcinolone, methylprednisolone) reduce allergic inflammation while local anesthetics (bupivacaine, lidocaine) provide symptomatic relief (pain/itch) via neural blockade; complementary mechanisms address the same disease manifestations.

Ketoconazole is the antifungal treating the primary superficial mycosis; dexamethasone reduces inflammatory symptoms; fusidic acid covers/prevents secondary bacterial infection—together address pathogen and inflammatory/complicating components of the condition.
Clavulanic acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that protects the β-lactam antibiotic ceftibuten from enzymatic degradation, enhancing antibacterial activity against pathogens causing pharyngitis.

These agents are combined in topical analgesic formulations for arthralgia and act via complementary analgesic/counterirritant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms (menthol TRPM8 cooling, camphor/TRP modulation, methyl salicylate salicylate analgesia, thymol/borneol additional analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects).

All agents are topical analgesics/essential oils that provide complementary pain-relief mechanisms (counterirritant cooling/warming via menthol/camphor/TRP channels, topical salicylate analgesia from methyl salicylate, anti-inflammatory/analgesic effects from eucalyptus/peppermint), acting together to relieve arthralgia.

Diclofenac (NSAID) reduces inflammation/prostaglandin-mediated pain while lidocaine (local anesthetic) blocks sodium channels to inhibit nociceptive signaling — complementary analgesic mechanisms for pain.

Menthol and camphor are topical counterirritants acting on sensory TRP channels to relieve pain; cetrimonium is an excipient/antimicrobial that can aid topical formulation/penetration. Together they target pain via complementary topical mechanisms.

All three agents are topical barrier/emollient/moisturizing agents used to treat exanthems by restoring skin barrier, retaining moisture and protecting against irritants; complementary mechanisms enhance symptomatic and barrier repair effects.

Thiocolchicoside is a muscle relaxant reducing involuntary muscle activity; ibuprofen is an NSAID reducing pain/inflammation that can contribute to or accompany hyperkinesia—complementary mechanisms addressing the same clinical manifestations.
Both salicylic acid and urea are topical keratolytics/moisturizers used to soften and remove hyperkeratotic lesions (keratoma); their combined use enhances keratolysis via complementary mechanisms.

Insufficient/ambiguous information: 'pirfotekh' identity unclear and stannous chloride is not a recognized standard therapy for gastrointestinal hemorrhage; no clear mechanistic synergy or side-effect mitigation is evident.

Chlorphenamine (antihistamine) reduces histamine-mediated secretion/inflammation and phenylephrine (alpha-agonist decongestant) reduces mucosal edema/vascular congestion; they act on complementary pathways to relieve upper airway/postnasal drip–related throat irritation.

Chlorphenamine is an antihistamine that directly relieves sneezing; salicylamide is an analgesic/antipyretic that treats pain/fever, not the sneeze mechanism — combination treats co-occurring symptoms rather than synergistically targeting sneezing.
